requirement: ## Requirement: MPS Op Coverage Tracking  **Background** The MPS backend supports only a subset of the framework's operators. Today there is no single, authoritative view of which ops are implemented, which are missing, and how well each is tested, so gaps are discovered ad hoc (user reports, failing tests) and coverage silently regresses over time.  **Requirement** The project shall maintain a machine-readable and human-readable inventory ("op coverage table") of all framework operators with respect to the MPS backend, and shall treat the inventory as a first-class, continuously validated artifact. requirement:
# Requirement: Inclusive Variant of `take_while` ## Summary Add a new iterator adaptor that behaves like `take_while`, but additionally yields the first element for which the predicate returns `false` (the "boundary" element). After yielding that boundary element, the iterator must terminate. ## Motivation `take_while` stops *before* the first element that fails the predicate, so callers who need to observe the terminating element must fall back to manual iteration (for example, a `while let` loop, or `peekable` handling) and re-implement the stop logic. An inclusive counterpart provides this behavior directly and consistently with the existing adaptor. ## Proposed API Add a method on `Iterator`: ``` fn take_while_inclusive

(self, predicate: P) -> TakeWhileInclusive where P: FnMut(&Self::Item) -> bool, ``` A corresponding free function in the iterator module may also be provided: ``` fn take_while_inclusive(iter: I, predicate: P) -> TakeWhileInclusive ``` ## Semantics Given a predicate `p` and an underlying iterator `I`: 1. For each element `x` produced by `I`, evaluate `p(&x)`. 2. If `p(&x)` is `true`, yield `x` and continue. 3. If `p(&x)` is `false`, yield `x` (the boundary element) and then return `None` on all subsequent calls to `next`. 4. If `I` is exhausted before any element fails `p`, the adaptor simply returns `None`. requirement: # Requirement: INT4 Data Format Support  ## 1. Summary The system shall support the INT4 (4-bit signed integer) numeric format as a first-class data type across the full data lifecycle: representation, parsing/serialization, storage, memory layout, and conversion to and from existing supported formats.  ## 2. Rationale INT4 reduces memory footprint and bandwidth by up to 8× relative to INT32 and 4× relative to INT8, enabling larger models/datasets and lower-latency execution on memory-constrained targets. Users currently must emulate INT4 externally, which is error-prone and prevents participation in standard pipelines.  ## 3. Scope **In scope** - INT4 type definition, including range, signedness, and overflow/underflow semantics. - Packing and unpacking of two 4-bit values per byte (and the defined handling of odd-length tensors/arrays). - Conversion (cast/quantize/dequantize) between INT4 and existing integer and floating-point formats. - Reading and writing INT4 data in all supported serialization and model-format paths. - Memory allocation, alignment, and strided access for INT4 buffers.  **Out of scope** - Sub-4-bit formats (e.g., INT2, ternary). - Changes to the numerical accuracy of existing formats. - Hardware-specific kernel optimization beyond correctness (performance targets addressed separately).  ## 4. Functional Requirements  | ID | Requirement | |----|-------------| | FR-1 | The system shall expose INT4 as a selectable data type through the same public API surface used for existing integer types. | | FR-2 | INT4 shall be a signed 4-bit integer with representable range −8 to +7. Unsigned 4-bit (UINT4, 0–15) support shall be provided if the type system already distinguishes signedness for other widths. | | FR-3 | Values shall be packed two-per-byte. The system shall define and document the nibble ordering (low nibble first) and the padding convention for odd element counts. | | FR-4 | Casting a value outside the INT4 range shall follow the library's established overflow policy for other narrowing integer casts; the chosen behavior (saturate or wrap) shall be documented and applied consistently. | | FR-5 | Casting between INT4 and INT8/INT16/INT32/INT64/FLOAT16/BFLOAT16/FLOAT32 shall be supported in both directions, with dequantization accepting an optional scale and zero-point for asymmetric quantization. | | FR-6 | All supported serialization paths shall be able to write and read INT4 tensors/arrays, preserving element values, shape, and packing layout on round-trip. | | FR-7 | INT4 buffers shall support the standard operations available to other dtypes: shape/stride queries, slicing, concatenation, reshape (where element count permits), and device/host transfer. | | FR-8 | Attempting to load an INT4 artifact on a build without INT4 support shall produce a clear, actionable error rather than silent corruption. |  ## 5. Non-Functional Requirements - **Correctness:** Round-trip conversion INT4 → INT8 → INT4 shall be lossless for all in-range values. - **Memory:** An INT4 tensor of N elements shall occupy ceil(N/2) bytes of payload, excluding metadata. - **Compatibility:** Existing formats and APIs shall remain source- and behavior-compatible; no existing default dtype shall change. - **Portability:** Behavior shall be identical across all supported CPU architectures and accelerator backends.  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria 1. A user can construct an INT4 tensor/array from a list of in-range integers and read back identical values. 2. Packing of an odd-length sequence (e.g., 5 elements) yields 3 bytes with a documented, deterministic padding nibble, and unpacks to exactly 5 elements. 3. Out-of-range input produces the documented saturation or wrap result, covered by unit tests at the boundaries −8, −9, +7, +8. 4. INT4 artifacts round-trip through save/load with bit-exact element values and identical shapes. 5. Interoperability test: an INT4 tensor produced by the system can be consumed by at least one external reference implementation, and vice versa, with matching values. 6. All new code paths are covered by automated tests, including error handling for unsupported builds.  ## 7. Assumptions and Open Questions - **Assumption:** "INT4" denotes a 4-bit integer quantization format; the requester is not referring to a PostgreSQL `int4` (32-bit) alias. *Confirm with requester.* - **Open:** Is symmetric quantization sufficient, or is asymmetric (scale + zero-point) required in the first iteration? - **Open:** Are group-wise/per-channel quantization granularities required, or only per-tensor? - **Open:** Which backends must be supported at initial release, and is a fallback reference implementation acceptable for the remainder?  ## 8. Dependencies - Type-system and dispatch-layer changes to register the new dtype. - Serialization/format specification updates and versioning of affected file formats. - Documentation updates: type reference, conversion semantics, packing layout, and migration notes.
explanation: The requirement is detailed and mostly clear, defining INT4 range, packing, conversion, and acceptance criteria, though some aspects (padding value, overflow policy) are left open, causing minor ambiguity. It provides concrete, measurable criteria enabling easy verification. The core capability is a single, well‑focused INT4 support, making it highly singular.

requirement: **Requirement: Zero-Copy Access to Shared Memory on NVIDIA Jetson Devices**  The software shall support zero-copy data exchange between CPU and GPU on NVIDIA Jetson devices that provide unified/shared memory, so that buffers already resident in shared memory can be accessed by both CPU and GPU without redundant host-to-device or device-to-host memory copies.  **Functional Requirements** 1. The software shall detect when it is running on an NVIDIA Jetson platform with shared CPU/GPU memory and determine whether zero-copy shared-memory access is available. 2. When zero-copy operation is enabled and supported, the software shall allocate or accept unified/shared-memory buffers and expose them to both CPU and GPU processing paths without performing unnecessary copy operations. 3. The software shall provide a configuration option to enable, disable, or automatically select zero-copy shared-memory behavior. 4. The software shall preserve buffer ownership, lifetime, alignment, and synchronization semantics for zero-copy buffers, including correct CPU/GPU access ordering through appropriate synchronization primitives. 5. The software shall fall back to the existing copy-based behavior on non-Jetson platforms, when shared memory is unavailable, when zero-copy is disabled, or when allocation/access fails. 6. The software shall report clear errors or warnings when zero-copy shared-memory operation cannot be used and shall not silently produce incorrect results. 7. The software shall release zero-copy resources correctly and avoid memory leaks, dangling references, or use-after-free conditions.  **Acceptance Criteria** 1. On a supported NVIDIA Jetson device with zero-copy enabled, a processing pipeline using shared-memory buffers completes without explicit CPU-to-GPU or GPU-to-CPU copy operations for those buffers. 2. Results produced through the zero-copy path are functionally identical to results produced through the existing copy-based path within defined numerical tolerances. 3. Disabling zero-copy or running on a non-Jetson platform preserves existing behavior through the fallback path. 4. Resource cleanup after zero-copy use shows no memory leaks or unreleased GPU/CPU mappings. 5. The feature can be enabled, disabled, and validated through documented configuration and runtime diagnostics.

provide structured logs and tracing hooks. 10. **Security:** Support authentication, authorization, TLS, request size limits, input validation, and secure model artifact loading. 11. **Deployment:** Provide Docker images, Kubernetes manifests or Helm charts, and configuration for local, cloud, and edge deployments. 12. **Extensibility:** Provide stable extension points for custom backends, protocols, serialization formats, and orchestration integrations. 13. **Client libraries:** Provide a Python client and examples for programmatic inference and management. 14. **Documentation:** Include quickstart guides, API references, end-to-end examples, and operational best practices.  **Non-Functional Requirements** - **Performance:** Achieve low-latency, high-throughput inference and scale horizontally. - **Reliability:** Support graceful shutdown, retries, fault isolation, and recovery from worker failures. - **Compatibility:** Work with supported PyTorch and Python versions. - **Usability:** Provide simple CLI and configuration, with minimal boilerplate for common deployment scenarios. - **Maintainability:** Be modular, tested, documented, and integrated with CI/CD. - **Licensing:** Use an open-source license compatible with the PyTorch ecosystem.  **Acceptance Criteria** - A user can package a trained PyTorch model, start the server, and invoke inference via HTTP and gRPC. - The server handles concurrent requests with configurable batching and reports operational metrics. - Multiple model versions can be deployed and switched without downtime. - The framework runs on CPU and GPU and scales in Kubernetes. - Documentation includes end-to-end examples and complete API references.

requirement: # Requirement: `DistributedSampler` SHALL Accept a `Sampler` as Input  **Component:** `torch.utils.data.distributed.DistributedSampler` **Type:** Feature enhancement (API extension) **Priority:** Medium **Backward compatibility:** Required  ## 1. Problem Statement  `DistributedSampler` is currently constructed exclusively from a `Dataset` and derives its index stream internally as `range(len(dataset))`. Users who wish to combine distributed sharding with an alternative index-selection strategy (e.g. a weighted, subset, class-balanced, curriculum, or user-defined `Sampler`) have no supported way to do so. They must either re-implement rank/`num_replicas` sharding, padding, and epoch-seeded shuffling themselves, or fork the class. This blocks composition of two independent, orthogonal concerns: *which* examples to draw, and *how* to split those examples across processes.  ## 2. Goal  Enable `DistributedSampler` to take any `torch.utils.data.Sampler` as its index source, sharding the indices produced by that sampler across the members of the distributed process group, with the same semantics it already provides for datasets.  ## 3. Scope  **In scope:** the `DistributedSampler` constructor, its index-generation and sharding behaviour, `set_epoch`, `__len__`, `__iter__`, error handling, type hints, and documentation.  **Out of scope:** changes to the `Sampler`/`Dataset` base classes, to `DataLoader`, to `BatchSampler`, to any other concrete sampler, and to distributed backends or process-group semantics.  ## 4. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Sampler input accepted.** The constructor's first positional parameter SHALL accept either a `Dataset` or a `Sampler` instance. The parameter SHALL be validated by type at construction time.  **FR-2 — Index source.** When a `Sampler` is supplied, the candidate indices SHALL be exactly the sequence of values produced by iterating that sampler. `DistributedSampler` SHALL invoke the wrapped sampler's `__iter__` at most once per call to its own `__iter__`. Indices MAY be arbitrary hashable values within the range consumed by `DataLoader`; the existing `int`-index convention SHALL be preserved in type hints (`Sampler[int]`).  **FR-3 — Sharding.** Sharding SHALL be applied to the sampler's output sequence as follows, where `I` is the index sequence and `N = len(I)`: - if `drop_last=True`: `num_samples = N // num_replicas`, and `I` SHALL be truncated to `num_samples * num_replicas`; - if `drop_last=False`: `num_samples = ceil(N / num_replicas)`, and `I` SHALL be padded to `num_samples * num_replicas` by cycling elements from the start of the sequence; - each rank `r` SHALL receive `I[r : total_size : num_replicas]`.  Each rank's subset SHALL be disjoint from every other rank's subset, and union over all ranks SHALL equal the truncated/padded sequence.  **FR-4 — Length.** `__len__` SHALL return the number of indices assigned to the current rank, i.e. `num_samples`, computed as in FR-3, and SHALL be consistent with the number of items yielded by `__iter__`.  **FR-5 — Shuffling.** When `shuffle=True`, the sequence returned by the wrapped sampler SHALL be deterministically permuted once per epoch using a generator seeded with `seed + epoch`, and the resulting permutation SHALL be identical on all ranks. When `shuffle=False`, the wrapped sampler's ordering SHALL be preserved verbatim. `DistributedSampler` SHALL NOT reseed or otherwise alter the internal randomness of the wrapped sampler; documentation SHALL state that determinism across ranks for stochastic samplers requires the user to supply a seeded generator to that sampler.  **FR-6 — Epoch tracking.** `set_epoch(epoch)` SHALL remain available and SHALL affect the permutation of FR-5. Its semantics SHALL be unchanged from the dataset-based path.  **FR-7 — Dataset path unchanged.** When a `Dataset` is supplied, behaviour, signatures, and outputs SHALL be byte-for-byte equivalent to the current implementation for all combinations of `num_replicas`, `rank`, `shuffle`, `seed`, and `drop_last`.  **FR-8 — Distributed defaults.** When a `Sampler` is supplied, `num_replicas` and `rank` SHALL default to `torch.distributed.get_world_size()` and `torch.distributed.get_rank()` respectively, identically to the dataset path.  **FR-9 — DataLoader interoperability.** A `DistributedSampler` wrapping a `Sampler` SHALL be usable as the `sampler` argument of `torch.utils.data.DataLoader`, including in combination with a user-supplied `batch_sampler`-independent configuration. Existing `DataLoader` validation rules SHALL continue to apply.  ## 5. Interface Specification  ```python class DistributedSampler(Sampler[int]):     def __init__(         self,         dataset: Union[Dataset, Sampler, None] = None,         num_replicas: Optional[int] = None,         rank: Optional[int] = None,         shuffle: bool = True,         seed: int = 0,         drop_last: bool = False,     ) -> None: ... ```  The first parameter SHALL be documented as "a dataset or a sampler to distribute"; its internal storage SHALL be exposed only through behaviour, not as a new public attribute.  ## 6. Edge Cases and Error Handling  - **FR-10** If the first argument is neither a `Dataset` nor a `Sampler`, construction SHALL raise `TypeError` with a message naming both accepted types. - **FR-11** If `num_replicas <= 0`, or `rank` is outside `[0, num_replicas)`, construction SHALL raise `ValueError` (existing behaviour preserved). - **FR-12** If `drop_last=True` and the sampler yields fewer than `num_replicas` indices, `__len__` SHALL return `0` and `__iter__` SHALL yield nothing, without raising. - **FR-13** If the wrapped sampler yields zero indices with `drop_last=False`, all ranks SHALL yield an empty sequence. - **FR-14** If `torch.distributed` is not initialized and `num_replicas`/`rank` are not supplied explicitly, the existing error behaviour SHALL be preserved (raise `RuntimeError` on `get_world_size`).  ## 7. Backward Compatibility  No existing public signature, parameter name, positional order, attribute, or return value SHALL change. All current usage patterns SHALL remain valid. No deprecation cycle is required, as the change is purely additive.  ## 8. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1** The dataset-based code path SHALL incur no measurable construction- or iteration-time regression (target: within 2% on the existing `DistributedSampler` benchmarks). - **NFR-2** Memory overhead SHALL be O(N) in the sampler's output length for `shuffle=True` and O(1) extra for `shuffle=False`. - **NFR-3** Public API documentation SHALL include an example combining `DistributedSampler` with a non-trivial sampler and a `DataLoader`. - **NFR-4** New behaviour SHALL be covered by unit tests, including multi-process tests validating disjointness and completeness across ranks.  ## 9. Acceptance Criteria  - **AC-1** Given a `Sampler` yielding 10 indices, `num_replicas=3`, `rank=0..2`, `drop_last=False`, each rank yields exactly 4 indices, the three sets are pairwise disjoint, and their union equals the padded sequence defined in FR-3. - **AC-2** Given the same configuration with `drop_last=True`, each rank yields exactly 3 indices and no padding occurs. - **AC-3** Given `DistributedSampler(some_sampler, shuffle=True, seed=S)` with the same epoch, all ranks produce the same base permutation before sharding. - **AC-4** Given `DistributedSampler(some_sampler, shuffle=False)`, rank `r`'s output equals every `num_replicas`-th element of the wrapped sampler's unmodified output, starting at offset `r`. - **AC-5** All pre-existing `DistributedSampler` tests pass unmodified. - **AC-6** Constructing with an invalid first argument raises `TypeError`; invalid `num_replicas`/`rank` raise `ValueError`. - **AC-7** A `DataLoader` whose `sampler` is a `DistributedSampler` wrapping a custom `Sampler` iterates successfully for a full epoch in a multi-process test.  ## 10. Assumptions  - A single `DistributedSampler` instance wraps exactly one index source; simultaneous dataset-plus-sampler construction is not required. - The wrapped sampler is re-iterable (implements `__iter__` returning a fresh iterator on each call). - Index values produced by the wrapped sampler are valid for the dataset later passed to `DataLoader`; validating that correspondence is the caller's responsibility.
explanation: The requirement is detailed and largely unambiguous, with precise functional and acceptance criteria, but some ambiguity remains around allowing arbitrary hashable indices and the definition of "range consumed by DataLoader", leading to a slightly lower unambiguity score. requirement: # Feature Requirement: First-Class SEO and Web Indexability for Flutter Web  ## Summary Flutter web shall provide documented, first-class support for generating crawler-accessible, route-aware HTML content and metadata so that search engines can discover, render, and index Flutter web applications without relying solely on client-side JavaScript execution.  ## Functional Requirements 1. **Crawler-accessible content**    - Flutter web builds shall support an SEO/prerender mode that emits standard HTML containing the primary visible content for each route, including text, headings, images with alt text, and navigable links.    - The emitted HTML shall not require JavaScript execution for search engines to identify the page’s primary content, title, description, canonical URL, and internal links.  2. **Route-aware metadata**    - The framework/tooling shall provide a supported mechanism for defining and emitting per-route SEO metadata, including at minimum:      - `<title>`      - meta description      - canonical URL      - robots directives      - Open Graph and Twitter Card metadata    - Metadata shall be correct for the requested route in both prerendered/static HTML and client-side navigation.  3. **Crawlable navigation**    - In-app navigation shall update the browser URL using real paths or hash routes as configured.    - Semantic link elements shall expose valid `href` values for navigable destinations so crawlers can discover routes.    - The SEO mode shall support generation of a sitemap or provide documented tooling to generate one from the app’s route configuration.  4. **Static HTML / prerendering support**    - Flutter web tooling shall support prerendering configured routes to static HTML at build time or serving time.    - Prerendered output shall include route-specific content and metadata and shall hydrate correctly into the interactive Flutter application.    - The feature shall be opt-in and shall not break existing Flutter web applications that do not enable it.  5. **Documentation and reference implementation**    - Official documentation shall describe how to enable SEO/prerendering, configure routes and metadata, generate sitemaps, and validate crawler output.    - A reference example application shall demonstrate a multi-route Flutter web app with indexable content and metadata.  ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A Flutter web app using the documented SEO configuration produces, for each configured route, HTML that contains:    - the route-specific title and meta description,    - the canonical URL,    - the primary page text and headings,    - at least one standard anchor element with a valid `href` for each navigable route. 2. Fetching a configured route with JavaScript disabled returns the route’s primary content and SEO metadata in the initial HTML response. 3. Client-side navigation to a configured route updates the document title, meta description, canonical URL, and URL path to match that route. 4. Prerendered pages hydrate into the interactive Flutter app without console errors or loss of route state. 5. Automated tests validate prerendered HTML output, route metadata, canonical URLs, and crawlable link generation. 6. Existing Flutter web applications that do not enable the SEO/prerender mode continue to build and behave as before.  ## Out of Scope - Guaranteed ranking improvements or search-engine ranking algorithms. - Server-side rendering for non-web Flutter targets. - Automatic content generation or SEO copywriting.

requirement: # Requirement: Support `compute` on a Separate Thread in Flutter Web  ## 1. Summary  `compute` (in `package:flutter/foundation.dart`) currently executes its callback on the main thread when the application targets the web, because Dart isolates are not available in the web runtime. This makes `compute` unable to fulfill its documented purpose on web: offloading CPU-intensive work so that the UI thread remains responsive. This requirement defines the behavior needed for `compute` to execute its callback off the main thread on Flutter Web, without changing the public API or breaking behavior on native platforms.  ## 2. Problem Statement  On native platforms, `compute` spawns an isolate and runs the callback in parallel with the main isolate. On Flutter Web, the existing implementation invokes the callback directly on the main thread. As a result, applications that use `compute` for heavy parsing, decoding, or computation experience dropped frames and unresponsive UI on web, contrary to the documented behavior of the API. Application code must currently be restructured with web-specific workarounds, and the framework provides no supported path to offload work on web.  ## 3. Scope  **In scope** - Off-main-thread execution of `compute` callbacks on the Flutter Web platform. - The `dart2js` and `dartwasm` compilation targets. - Preserving the existing `compute` API and its semantics on native platforms. - Behavior when off-main-thread execution is not available at runtime.  **Out of scope** - General isolate support (`dart:isolate`, `Isolate.run`, `Isolate.spawn`) on the web. - Shared-memory parallelism (`SharedArrayBuffer`/`Atomics`) or shared mutable state between threads. - Cancellation of in-flight `compute` calls. - Changes to native-platform threading behavior or performance characteristics.  ## 4. Functional Requirements  - **FR-1.** `compute<M, R>(ComputeCallback<M, R> callback, M message, {DebugLabel? debugLabel})` shall execute `callback` on a thread other than the main/UI thread when running on Flutter Web in a supported environment. - **FR-2.** The public signature, name, return type, and positional/named parameters of `compute` shall remain unchanged. No breaking API changes are permitted on any platform. - **FR-3.** `compute` shall return a `Future<R>` that completes with the callback's return value once the callback has finished executing off the main thread. - **FR-4.** If the callback throws, the returned `Future` shall complete with an error carrying the thrown object. The error shall be propagated to the caller on the main thread with an equivalent error type and message, and with stack-trace information preserved to the extent the platform permits. - **FR-5.** The implementation shall use Web Workers as the off-main-thread mechanism, since Dart isolates are unavailable on the web. - **FR-6.** `message` shall be delivered to the callback as an argument, and the result shall be returned to the caller, using a structured-clone-compatible transport. `compute` shall document these constraints in its API documentation. - **FR-7.** If `message` or the callback's return value cannot be transferred (e.g., it contains a function, a DOM node, a closed-over object, or another non-serializable value), `compute` shall fail with a clear, actionable error identifying the offending value or type, rather than silently returning an incorrect or degraded result. - **FR-8.** `compute` shall continue to require the callback to be a top-level or static function. Invoking `compute` with a closure or instance method shall produce a clear error at the earliest point possible. - **FR-9.** Multiple `compute` calls may be in flight concurrently. Concurrent calls shall not serialize behind one another in a way that prevents independent callbacks from making progress, and no call shall block the main thread while its callback runs. - **FR-10.** Worker resources shall be managed so that repeated `compute` calls do not incur unbounded resource growth. Worker startup cost shall be amortized where feasible (e.g., by reusing workers), and workers shall be released when no longer needed. - **FR-11.** If off-main-thread execution is unavailable at runtime (e.g., the environment does not support Web Workers, or the app runs in a restricted context), `compute` shall fall back to executing the callback on the main thread so that functional correctness is preserved. The fallback shall not throw or silently return an incorrect result. - **FR-12.** `compute` shall preserve its existing behavior on native platforms; the web implementation shall not alter native code paths. - **FR-13.** The API documentation for `compute` shall be updated to describe the web behavior, including the serialization constraints and the conditions under which the main-thread fallback applies.  ## 5. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 (Responsiveness).** While a `compute` callback is executing on web, the main thread shall remain available to the framework's event loop. Long-running callbacks (e.g., a CPU-bound loop of at least one second) shall not prevent the UI from rendering frames or handling input. - **NFR-2 (Compatibility).** The web implementation shall work under both the `dart2js` and `dartwasm` compilation targets and across current evergreen browsers that support Web Workers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge). - **NFR-3 (Backward compatibility).** Existing applications that call `compute` shall continue to compile and run on all platforms without source changes. - **NFR-4 (Testability).** `compute`'s off-main-thread behavior shall be exercisable from the Flutter web test environments used by the framework's own test suites and by application authors. - **NFR-5 (Observability).** When the main-thread fallback is used, the framework shall provide a debuggable signal (e.g., a debug-mode diagnostic or documentation-covered condition) explaining why off-main-thread execution was not used. - **NFR-6 (Documented costs).** Documentation shall state that serialization overhead is incurred per call, so that passing large payloads is not assumed to be cheaper than computing on the main thread.  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria  1. On Flutter Web, a `compute` call whose callback busy-loops for at least one second does not block the main thread: an animation or other continuous UI work scheduled on the main thread continues to produce frames during the call. 2. The value returned by `compute` on web equals the value returned by the same callback on a native platform for structured-clone-compatible inputs. 3. A callback that throws causes the returned `Future` to complete with an error whose message matches the thrown error, on web as well as on native platforms. 4. Passing a non-serializable `message` or returning a non-serializable result produces an explicit, descriptive error. 5. In an environment without Web Worker support, `compute` still returns the correct result via the main-thread fallback. 6. A loop of many sequential `compute` calls completes without unbounded growth in worker or memory resources. 7. All existing `compute` tests for native platforms continue to pass unchanged.  ## 7. Assumptions, Dependencies, and Risks  - **Dependencies.** Web Worker bindings available to the Flutter web engine (e.g., via `dart:js_interop`/`package:web`), and build tooling capable of compiling and loading the worker entrypoint alongside the application. - **Assumption.** Callers accept that web off-thread execution requires structured-clone-compatible arguments and results, matching the existing `compute` contract that the callback must be a top-level or static function. - **Risk.** Environments that disable or lack Web Workers (including some embedded webviews and test harnesses) cannot offer off-thread execution; FR-11 defines the required degradation so behavior stays correct even where performance cannot be improved. - **Risk.** Serialization overhead can make `compute` slower than main-thread execution for small payloads; this must be documented rather than hidden.

requirement: # Requirement: DRM Content Playback Support in `video_player`  ## Summary The `video_player` plugin shall support playback of DRM-protected media streams on all supported platforms by allowing applications to supply platform-appropriate DRM configuration (license acquisition endpoints, authentication headers, and content identifiers) when initializing a video source, and by correctly performing license acquisition, decryption, and playback through the underlying platform media stack.  ## Scope - **In scope:** Widevine (Android, and Android-based platforms), FairPlay Streaming (iOS, macOS), PlayReady (Windows), and ClearKey (all platforms) for HLS and DASH streams. - **Out of scope:** DRM key server implementations, content packaging/encryption tooling, and persistent offline license storage.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **DRM configuration API**    - The plugin shall expose a public, platform-agnostic API that accepts a DRM configuration object alongside the media URL when creating a video source.    - The configuration object shall support, at minimum:      - `drmType` (e.g., `widevine`, `fairplay`, `playready`, `clearkey`).      - `licenseUrl`: the license acquisition endpoint.      - `headers`: HTTP headers required for license requests (e.g., authorization tokens).      - `assetId` / `contentId`: identifier required by the license server, where applicable.      - `certificateUrl`: FairPlay application certificate URL (iOS/macOS only).    - The API shall be additive and shall not break existing `VideoPlayerController` construction for non-DRM content.  2. **License acquisition and playback**    - On Android, the plugin shall pass DRM configuration to ExoPlayer/Media3 via `MediaItem.DrmConfiguration`, enabling Widevine and ClearKey license requests.    - On iOS and macOS, the plugin shall support FairPlay Streaming by fetching the application certificate, generating the SPC, obtaining the CKC from the license server, and supplying it to `AVAssetResourceLoaderDelegate`.    - On Windows, the plugin shall configure PlayReady through the platform media pipeline.    - The plugin shall select the appropriate DRM scheme for the target platform without requiring conditional logic in application code where a single configuration can be mapped.  3. **Unsupported combinations**    - When a requested DRM scheme is not supported on the current platform, the plugin shall fail initialization with a descriptive error rather than silently failing or throwing an opaque platform exception.  4. **Error reporting**    - License acquisition failures (network errors, non-2xx responses, invalid license payloads) shall surface as a typed error through the existing `VideoPlayerController` error channel, including the HTTP status code and a human-readable message where available.  5. **Multiple video sources**    - DRM configuration shall be supported for each source passed to the plugin's source-list / concatenation APIs, so that mixed DRM and non-DRM playlists can be played.  ## Non-Functional Requirements  1. **Backward compatibility:** Existing public APIs and behavior for non-DRM content shall remain unchanged. 2. **Platform parity:** The API surface shall be consistent across platforms; only platform-specific fields (e.g., FairPlay certificate URL) may be conditionally required. 3. **Documentation:** Public API documentation shall include per-platform setup instructions (manifest changes, entitlements, capabilities) and a working example for at least one DRM scheme per platform. 4. **Testability:** The plugin shall include integration tests or documented manual test procedures using publicly available DRM test streams (e.g., Widevine/FairPlay test assets).  ## Acceptance Criteria  - requirement: # Requirement: PlatformView Support on macOS  ## Summary Flutter on macOS shall support PlatformView, enabling Flutter applications and plugins to embed native AppKit views (`NSView`) directly in the Flutter widget tree. Flutter gesture recognizers configured on the platform view shall be able to intercept or participate in hit testing. - **FR-9:** Platform view lifecycle shall be managed correctly: creation, reuse where applicable, disposal when removed from the widget tree, and cleanup on hot restart. Native resources shall not leak. - **FR-10:** Multiple platform views shall be supported simultaneously in a single Flutter view hierarchy. - **FR-11:** Platform views shall function in debug, profile, and release modes. - **FR-12:** Documentation and at least one example shall be provided showing how to implement a macOS platform view plugin.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - **AC-1:** Given a macOS Flutter app and a plugin registering a platform view factory, when Dart renders `AppKitView(viewType: 'example')`, the registered native `NSView` is created and displayed at the expected location and size. - **AC-2:** Resizing the macOS window updates the platform view’s native frame to match the Flutter widget bounds. - **AC-3:** Mouse clicks, drags, scroll events, and keyboard input reach the native view when the platform view is focused or hit-tested. - **AC-4:** Flutter gesture recognizers attached to the platform view can receive gestures according to the documented hit-test behavior. - **AC-5:** Two or more platform views can be displayed simultaneously and maintain correct ordering relative to Flutter widgets and each other. - **AC-6:** Removing the platform view widget from the tree disposes the native view and releases associated resources. - **AC-7:** Hot restart and hot reload do not leave orphaned native views or crash the application. - **AC-8:** VoiceOver and other accessibility features can access the native view, or any limitation is explicitly documented. - **AC-9:** Integration tests exist and pass on macOS for creation, layout, input, disposal, and multiple-view scenarios. - **AC-10:** Existing macOS rendering, input, and plugin behavior are not regressed.  ## Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1:** The implementation shall follow existing Flutter PlatformView API conventions for consistency with Android and iOS. - **NFR-2:** The feature shall not introduce continuous CPU or GPU usage when platform views are idle. - **NFR-3:** The implementation shall avoid memory leaks and native resource leaks. - **NFR-4:** The feature shall be supported on macOS versions covered by Flutter’s current macOS support policy. - **NFR-5:** Public APIs shall be documented and covered by tests.  ## Dependencies  - Flutter framework - Flutter engine - macOS embedder - AppKit / Cocoa - Flutter plugin registration APIs  ## Out of Scope  - PlatformView support on Windows, Linux, or web. - Changes to Android or iOS PlatformView behavior. - Full parity with Android hybrid composition if the macOS compositing model requires documented differences.

requirement: # Requirement: Release-Mode Builds on Simulators  ## Summary The build and run tooling SHALL support building and launching mobile applications in release mode on simulator/emulator targets, in addition to the currently supported debug and profile modes.  ## Motivation Release-mode behavior (optimized code, tree-shaking, disabled assertions, release-only configuration and error handling) often differs materially from debug-mode behavior. Developers currently cannot validate release-mode behavior without a physical device, which slows down diagnosis of release-only defects (e.g., rendering, performance, plugin, and networking issues) and increases reliance on CI or device hardware.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **Mode–Target Compatibility**    - The toolchain SHALL treat release mode as a valid build mode for simulator and emulator targets.    - Invoking a run/build command with release mode and a simulator target SHALL NOT fail with a "release mode not supported for simulators" error.  2. **Artifact Generation**    - The build pipeline SHALL produce a release-mode application bundle that is installable and launchable on the target simulator/emulator.    - Where the target architecture cannot support the standard release compilation strategy, the pipeline SHALL select an appropriate supported compilation strategy and document which optimizer/compilation configurations are unavailable.  3. **Runtime Semantics**    - Any semantic differences that cannot be reproduced on simulators SHALL be reported to the user before or during the run, identifying the affected capabilities.  4. **Configuration**    - Release-mode-specific configuration, entry points, and environment definitions (e.g., release flavor/variant settings) SHALL be applied identically on simulator targets as on device targets, except where explicitly unsupported.  5. **User Feedback**    - Where a release-mode simulator build succeeds but with degraded fidelity relative to device release builds, the tooling SHALL emit a non-fatal notice enumerating the differences.  6. **Diagnostics**    - Release-mode simulator runs SHALL support the standard attach/detach, structured logging, and crash/stack-trace symbolication paths available for device release builds, to the extent the platform permits.  ## Non-Functional Requirements  - **Performance:** Release-mode simulator builds SHALL reflect the optimizations applicable to the selected compilation strategy; documented performance characteristics SHALL be published where they diverge from device release builds. - **Compatibility:** Existing debug and profile simulator workflows, and existing release-mode device workflows, SHALL remain unaffected. - **Documentation:** User-facing documentation SHALL state supported mode/target combinations and any known fidelity gaps for release-mode simulator builds.  ## Acceptance Criteria  1. Running the application on an iOS Simulator in release mode completes successfully and launches the app. 2. Running the application on an Android Emulator in release mode completes successfully and launches the app. 3. The launched release-mode simulator build reports release mode, with assertions disabled and debug-only UI elements absent. 4. A failure case (unsupported configuration) produces a message identifying the specific unsupported element. 5. Debug and profile simulator builds, and release device builds, continue to behave as before.  ## Out of Scope  - Changes to platform vendor simulator/emulator limitations that are outside the project's control. - Guaranteeing bit-for-bit identical behavior or performance between simulator release builds and device release builds.

requirement: # Software Requirement: Replace GridMap with an Improved TileMap3D Node  ## Summary Replace the existing `GridMap` node with a new node named `TileMap3D` that adopts the architecture and workflow of the redesigned 2D `TileMap` node. Provide a new `Node3D`-derived class named `TileMap3D` for placing tiles on a 3D grid.    - The node shall mirror the conceptual API and behavior of the 2D `TileMap` node, adapted to three dimensions.  2. **TileSet-Based Resource Model**    - `TileMap3D` shall be driven by a `TileSet3D` resource, structured analogously to the 2D `TileSet`.    - `TileSet3D` shall support:      - Tile sources (equivalent to `TileSetScenesCollectionSource`, atlas-style sources, and mesh-based sources).      - Per-tile metadata, custom data layers, and collision information.      - Per-tile configuration of mesh instances, materials, and transforms.    - Existing `MeshLibrary` resources shall be convertible to `TileSet3D` via an import path or migration tool.  3. **Layering**    - `TileMap3D` shall support multiple independently configurable tile layers.    - Each layer shall expose: visibility, Z-index/ordering, transform, collision enable/disable, and per-layer cell size and origin.  4. **Terrain and Autotiling**    - `TileSet3D` shall support terrain sets equivalent to the 2D terrain/autotile system (bitmask and/or minimal matching modes).    - `TileMap3D` shall support automatic terrain painting consistent with 2D behavior.  5. **Editing Workflow**    - The TileMap3D editor shall provide painting, erasing, line, rectangle, and bucket-fill tools, mirroring the 2D TileMap editor.    - The editor shall support pattern selection, randomization, and probability-weighted placement.    - The 3D editor shall support snapping to grid cells and previewing tiles in the viewport.  6. **Runtime API**    - Provide runtime methods equivalent in intent to 2D `TileMap`: `set_cell`, `get_cell_source_id`, `erase_cell`, `clear_layer`, `map_to_local`/`local_to_map`, `set_layer_*`, and cell coordinate conversions between 2D grid coordinates and 3D positions.    - Support efficient bulk operations and dirty-region updates to avoid full relayouts.  7. **Compatibility and Migration**    - `GridMap` shall be marked deprecated and remain available for at least one release cycle.    - Provide a documented migration path from `GridMap`/`MeshLibrary` to `TileMap3D`/`TileSet3D`, including automated conversion where feasible.  ## Non-Functional Requirements - Performance for large maps (e.g., tens of thousands of cells) shall be at least on par with `GridMap`. - API naming and semantics shall remain consistent with the 2D `TileMap`/`TileSet` to the extent the 3D domain permits. - Documentation shall cover the new node, resource, migration, and editor usage.  ## Acceptance Criteria - A `TileMap3D` node can be added, associated with a `TileSet3D`, painted in the editor, and rendered correctly at runtime. - Terrain/autotiling functions in 3D as it does in 2D. - Multiple layers render and collide independently per their configuration. - A `GridMap` scene can be migrated to `TileMap3D` without manual reconstruction of tile data. - Existing `GridMap` projects continue to load and run while deprecation remains in effect.

requirement: # Requirement: Explicit Interface Definition in GDScript  ## Summary GDScript shall support the explicit declaration of **interfaces** — named contracts that specify a set of required method signatures (and optionally properties/signals) — and shall support statically verifying that any class declaring an interface fully implements it. Interfaces shall be usable as types for variables, parameters, return values, and exported properties.  ## Motivation GDScript currently expresses contracts only through duck typing, informal conventions, or abstract base classes. There is no way to declare a named contract that a class explicitly "implements," nor to type a value as "any object that fulfills this contract." As a result, contract violations surface only at runtime, tooling/autocompletion is limited, and expected APIs are poorly documented. An explicit interface construct enables earlier error detection, better editor tooling, and self-documenting APIs.  ## Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Interface declaration** - GDScript shall provide syntax to declare an interface as a named, first-class language construct (e.g., `interface IFoo:`). - An interface body shall contain method signatures with typed parameters and typed return values. - An interface shall contain no implementation bodies. - An interface may declare required properties and/or signals. - An interface may extend one or more other interfaces and shall inherit all of their requirements.  **FR-2 — Interface implementation** - A class shall be able to explicitly declare that it implements one or more interfaces. - A class may implement multiple interfaces. - An implementing class must provide a concrete implementation for every method signature declared by the interface(s), with compatible parameter and return types.  **FR-3 — Static verification** - The GDScript compiler shall verify at parse/compile time that every class declaring an interface satisfies all interface requirements. - A missing or signature-incompatible member shall produce a compile-time error that identifies the interface and the offending member.  **FR-4 — Interfaces as types** - Interfaces shall be usable as types for variables, function parameters, function return values, and exported properties. - Assigning a value to an interface-typed location shall require the value's class to implement that interface; the check shall be performed statically where determinable, otherwise at runtime. - The `is` and `as` operators, and type casting, shall accept interface types.  **FR-5 — Introspection** - The engine shall expose whether a class or object implements a given interface through reflection/introspection APIs.  **FR-6 — Editor tooling** - The editor shall provide autocompletion, documentation, and error highlighting for interfaces and their members.  ## Constraints and Non-Functional Requirements - **Backward compatibility:** The feature is additive; all existing GDScript projects must continue to compile and run unchanged. - **Performance:** Static verification shall impose no runtime overhead; runtime interface checks shall be efficient. - **Integration:** The construct shall interoperate with the existing inheritance model and the `class_name` registration system.  ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A script can declare an interface containing method signatures. 2. A script can declare that it implements one or more interfaces and is accepted only when all required members are implemented. 3. A variable, parameter, return value, or exported property can be typed as an interface and accepts any object whose class implements it. 4. Omitting or mismatching a required member produces a clear compile-time error naming the interface and member. 5. `is`/`as` checks and casts against interface types behave correctly at runtime. 6. Introspection APIs correctly report interface implementation. 7. All pre-existing GDScript code compiles and runs without modification.

However, the requirement bundles many distinct capabilities (declaration, implementation, verification, typing, introspection, tooling) rather than focusing on a single atomic capability, resulting in low singularity (score 2).

requirement: **Requirement: Built-in 2D Sprite Masking**  The engine shall provide a built-in 2D masking mechanism that allows `Sprite2D` and other `CanvasItem` nodes to be masked by another 2D texture or node without custom shaders. The feature shall be exposed through at least one of the following APIs:  1. **`Mask2D` node** — a new `Node2D`-derived node that masks its child `CanvasItem` nodes using the alpha channel of its rendered texture/shape. 2. **`mask_parent` property on `Sprite2D`** — a `NodePath` property that references a `Mask2D` or other `CanvasItem` whose rendered alpha channel defines the visible region of the `Sprite2D`.  **Functional requirements:** - Masking shall use the mask node’s alpha channel. By default, final pixel alpha shall be `source_alpha × mask_alpha`. An optional binary/clip mode may apply an adjustable alpha cutoff threshold. - The mask shall respect its own transform, rotation, scale, modulate, z-index, and canvas layer. - Pixels outside the mask texture/shape shall be fully transparent. - Only designated nodes shall be affected: children of a `Mask2D`, or nodes referencing a mask via `mask_parent`. Unrelated sibling/non-designated nodes shall not be affected. - Nested masks shall compose multiplicatively. - The feature shall work identically in the editor and at runtime, updating immediately when the mask or masked node is moved, animated, or modified. - The implementation shall not require per-frame CPU readback and should preserve batching where possible. - Existing projects shall remain unaffected unless the new node/property is used. - Documentation and automated tests shall be provided.  **Acceptance criteria:** - A `Sprite2D` masked by a `Mask2D` displays only within the mask’s alpha region. - Changing the mask’s transform, rotation, scale, or texture updates the masked result immediately in the editor and at runtime. - A `Sprite2D` with `mask_parent` set to a valid mask node produces the same masked output as the `Mask2D` child-node approach. - Disabling the mask node renders masked items unmasked, or follows the documented behavior for mask activation. - The feature is usable from GDScript and C# and is configurable through the editor inspector.

requirement: **Requirement:** GDScript shall support f-string literals. requirement: # Feature Requirement: Trait System for GDScript  ## Summary Add first-class support for traits to GDScript: a declaration construct that lets a script reuse a named, statically-checked bundle of members (methods, constants, signals, and properties) without using single inheritance. Traits are composed into a script at compile time via a `uses` clause, and the GDScript parser, analyzer, compiler, and editor tooling must all understand them.  ## Motivation GDScript currently supports only single inheritance (`extends`) plus inner classes. There is no sanctioned way to share implementation across unrelated classes, forcing code duplication or deep, brittle inheritance chains. A trait system provides horizontal code reuse while preserving GDScript's static analysis guarantees.  ## Functional Requirements  ### R1 — Trait declaration 1. A new top-level keyword `trait` shall declare a trait: `trait TraitName:` followed by an indented body. 2. A trait body shall permit the same member kinds as a class body: methods, constants, signals, properties (with getters/setters), and nested inner classes, subject to R6. 3. A trait shall support an optional `extends TraitName` clause to inherit from another trait (trait-to-trait inheritance only). 4. A trait shall not be instantiable; `TraitName.new()` shall be a parse/analysis error. 5. A trait shall not be usable as a type annotation; using a trait name where a type is expected shall produce an analysis error.  ### R2 — Trait composition 1. A class (or inner class) shall compose traits using a `uses TraitA, TraitB` clause placed after the optional `extends` clause. 2. `uses` shall accept one or more trait names separated by commas. 3. A trait may itself include a `uses` clause; traits are therefore transitively composable. Composition shall be resolved to a fixed set of members per class at analysis time (no runtime dispatch indirection required). 4. A class that `uses` a trait shall be assignable to and from that trait's own base classes where applicable (i.e., trait inheritance contributes its inherited members, but does not alter the using class's `extends` chain). 5. Circular trait composition (`A uses B`, `B uses A`) shall be detected and reported as an analysis error.  ### R3 — Member resolution 1. Members declared directly in the using class shall take precedence over members supplied by traits. 2. A member supplied by exactly one used trait shall be added to the class automatically. 3. If two used traits supply a member with the same name, and the class does not define it, this shall be a compile-time error naming both traits and the conflicting member. 4. The conflict in R3.3 may be resolved by the class defining the member itself, or by an explicit alias directive `use TraitName.Member as OtherName` within the class body. 5. Constants, signals, and property names shall follow the same conflict and precedence rules as methods.  ### R4 — Semantics of composed members 1. `self` inside a trait method shall refer to the instance of the using class. 2. Trait methods shall be able to call methods and access members defined by the using class, resolved at analysis time; referencing a member that no using class provides shall be reported as an error at the point where analysis can determine it, or deferred to composition-time checking. 3. Traits may declare abstract method requirements (a method signature with no body). Every class that `uses` such a trait must provide a concrete implementation, either directly or through another used trait; otherwise analysis shall fail. 4. Trait properties shall behave as if declared in the using class, including their getters, setters, and initializers. 5. `_init` and `_static_init` shall not be permitted in a trait body; a class's own initializers remain the only initialization entry points.  ### R5 — Reflection and tooling 1. A script shall expose a `get_traits()` method (or equivalent) returning the names of directly used traits; static analysis should expose the same information to the editor. 2. The editor shall provide go-to-definition, documentation lookup, and completion for members contributed by traits, attributing each member to its source trait. 3. The built-in documentation generator shall document traits and list, for each class, the traits it uses.  ### R6 — Restrictions 1. Traits shall not declare `class_name`; they are referenced by their script path or by name within the same file. 2. Traits shall not be `@tool`-qualified independently; `@tool` behavior is governed by the using class. 3. Traits shall not participate in `is`/`as` type checks as standalone types; the existing `extends` chain is unchanged. 4. Serialization, signal connections, and property replication shall operate on the using class's composed member set exactly as if those members had been written in the class.  ## Non-Functional Requirements 1. The feature shall preserve GDScript's existing static-typing guarantees: all trait member resolution exceptions shall be surfaced at parse/analysis time, not at runtime. 2. Composing traits shall not introduce per-call runtime lookup overhead beyond what an equivalent method declared directly in the class would incur. 3. Existing scripts without `uses` clauses shall parse and behave identically; the feature must be backward compatible. 4. Error messages for trait misuse (duplicate members, circular use, unimplemented abstract methods, non-instantiable traits) shall identify the trait, member, and source location.  ## Out of Scope - Runtime/dynamic trait addition or removal. - Traits as generic type parameters. - Multiple inheritance of classes. - Trait support in GDExtension/C# scripts.  ## Acceptance Criteria 1. A script declaring `trait Walkable:` with a `walk()` method, used via `uses Walkable`, compiles and exposes `walk()` on instances; calling `walk()` from a caller dispatches to the class instance. 2. Two traits defining the same method name produce an analysis error unless the class overrides the method or aliases one trait's member with `use`. 3. A trait that `extends` another trait contributes both sets of members to the using class, and `self` inside inherited trait methods resolves to the using instance. 4. A trait declaring an abstract method fails analysis on a using class that does not implement it, and passes on one that does. 5. `TraitName.new()` and a trait name used as a type hint each produce a clear analysis error. 6. Editor completion and go-to-definition resolve trait-contributed members to their defining trait. 7. A project with no `uses` clauses builds unchanged, and the GDScript test suite passes.
explanation: The requirement is detailed, precise, and clearly defines the trait system with explicit rules, making it unambiguous and verifiable; it focuses on a single feature.

It shall coexist with existing allocating APIs without breaking source or binary compatibility, be usable in editor and exported projects, and include automated tests proving zero managed allocations per operation after warm-up. Documentation shall cover usage, lifetime, threading, and disposal rules. Existing allocating convenience APIs shall remain available.  **Acceptance Criteria:** 1. API works in editor and exported projects on supported Godot platforms.

requirement: **Requirement: Script Editor Symbol Rename Refactoring**  The script editor shall provide a refactoring tool that allows users to rename a symbol—including variables, constants, functions, methods, classes, signals, enums, enum values, properties, and parameters—and automatically update all references to that symbol within the selected scope. The tool shall be accessible via a “Refactor” menu or submenu, the editor context menu, the command palette, and a configurable keyboard shortcut when the caret is on or a symbol is selected.  **Acceptance Criteria**  1. Invoking “Rename Symbol” opens an inline edit field or dialog pre-filled with the current symbol name. 2. The new name is validated against the scripting language’s identifier rules and checked for conflicts with existing symbols in the applicable scope; invalid or conflicting names prevent completion and display a clear error. 3. The user can select the refactoring scope: current script, open scripts, or entire project, where supported by the language and project structure. The default scope is the current script. 4. The tool identifies and updates all static references to the symbol in the selected scope, including declarations and usages, while preserving formatting, comments, and string literals unless the user explicitly opts to update them. 5. A preview of all affected files and changes is shown before applying, with the ability to include or exclude individual occurrences. 6. The feature is covered by automated tests for valid renames, name conflicts, scope selection, preview, undo/redo, and error handling.

requirement: **Requirement: Rendering Compositor**  The system SHALL implement a rendering compositor that accepts one or more rendered layers, composites them into a single output frame, and presents that frame through the active display/rendering backend. The compositor SHALL:  1. Maintain a mutable ordered layer list or tree. Each layer SHALL define at least: unique identifier, source surface/texture, bounds, z-order, visibility, opacity, transform, clip rectangle, and blend mode. 2. Composite layers in back-to-front z-order using source-over alpha blending with premultiplied alpha. Unsupported blend modes SHALL be rejected or fall back to source-over with a logged warning. 3. Apply per-layer transforms, clipping, and opacity before blending. Clipping SHALL constrain both sampling and output to the clip rectangle. 4. Support atomic layer updates: add, remove, reorder, show/hide, and property changes. Changes SHALL take effect on the next composited frame without restarting the compositor. 5. Track damage regions per layer where provided. If damage tracking is available, recomposite only affected regions; otherwise, composite the full output frame. The compositor SHALL never display partial or torn frames. 6. Synchronize composition and presentation with the rendering backend's frame/vsync mechanism. Layer mutations from other threads SHALL be synchronized so the compositor never reads partially updated layer state. 7. Prefer GPU-accelerated composition when available. Provide a CPU fallback path for environments without GPU support. Both paths SHALL produce visually equivalent output within the project's defined color and format tolerances. 8. Expose a programmatic API to create, update, remove, reorder, and query layers, and to start/stop the compositor. 9. Handle errors gracefully: invalid layer properties, missing source surfaces, unsupported formats, and backend failures SHALL be logged and SHALL NOT crash the process. If the primary backend fails, the compositor SHALL attempt fallback or stop cleanly. 10. Meet the project's frame budget on the documented reference hardware: composite and present a 1920x1080 frame at 60 Hz (16.6 ms/frame) with compositor overhead not exceeding 25% of the frame budget. Lower resolutions and refresh rates SHALL scale accordingly. 11. Include unit tests for z-ordering, alpha blending, opacity, transforms, clipping, damage-region updates, and error handling; and an integration test that composites multiple layers and verifies the final output against a reference image. 12. Document the compositor's layer model, API, supported blend modes and formats, and backend fallback behavior.  Acceptance criteria: the compositor builds and runs on supported platforms; the integration test passes; no tearing or crash occurs during layer mutation; the performance target is met on reference hardware; and CPU and GPU outputs match within the defined tolerance.

requirement: **Requirement: Implement a first-class Set primitive.**  The system shall provide a built-in `Set` type as a core primitive alongside the existing `Array` and `Dictionary` types. The `Set` shall represent a collection of unique values, complementing `Array` (ordered sequence) and `Dictionary` (key-value mapping) by providing efficient uniqueness, membership testing, and set-algebra operations.  **Functional requirements**  1. **Construction**    - A `Set` shall be constructible as empty, from an iterable such as an `Array`, or as a copy of another `Set`.    - A typed `Set` shall be constructible with an element type constraint, and an untyped `Set` shall accept any supported value type.  2. **Uniqueness**    - A `Set` shall not contain duplicate elements.    - Adding an element that is already present shall leave the `Set` unchanged and shall not increase its size.  3. **Core operations**    - The `Set` shall support adding, removing, and checking membership of an element.    - The `Set` shall expose its size, emptiness state, and a clear operation.    - The `Set` shall support iteration over its elements exactly once per element.  4. **Set algebra**    - The `Set` shall support union, intersection, difference, and symmetric difference.    - The `Set` shall support subset, superset, and disjointness checks.    - Set-algebra operations shall return new `Set` instances without mutating their operands unless an explicitly named in-place variant is used.  5. **Equality and comparison**    - Two `Set` instances shall be equal if and only if they contain the same elements, independent of insertion or iteration order.    - Iteration order shall be deterministic for a given `Set` instance and implementation, but shall not affect equality.  6. **Typed sets**    - A typed `Set` shall enforce its element type at runtime.    - Adding an element of an incompatible type to a typed `Set` shall raise an error consistent with existing typed `Array` and `Dictionary` behavior.  7. **Serialization and Variant integration**    - A `Set` shall be serializable and deserializable as a Variant without data loss, preserving its elements and type metadata.    - A `Set` shall be usable in the same contexts as `Array` and `Dictionary`, including scripting, engine APIs, property inspection, and documentation.  8. **Interoperability**    - A `Set` shall be convertible to and from an `Array`.    - Conversion from an `Array` containing duplicates shall produce a `Set` with duplicates removed.  9. **Performance**    - Membership testing, insertion, and removal shall have average-case time complexity no worse than O(1) for supported hashable element types.  10. **Error handling**     - Invalid operations, including type violations and unsupported element values, shall report errors consistently with existing collection types.  **Acceptance criteria**  - A `Set` can be created, populated, iterated, and serialized/deserialized without data loss. - Adding duplicate elements does not increase the `Set` size. - Union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference, subset, superset, and disjointness operations produce correct results. - Typed `Set` instances reject elements of incompatible types. - `Set` equality is order-independent and correct for identical element collections. - The `Set` type is documented, tested, and available through the same public APIs as `Array` and `Dictionary`.

requirement: # Requirement: Rustdoc Support for Per-Parameter Documentation  **Identifier:** RUSTDOC-PARAM-DOC-001 **Status:** Proposed **Priority:** Medium  ## 1. Summary  The Rust compiler and rustdoc shall support attaching documentation to individual parameters of callable items and shall render that documentation as structured, addressable output in generated documentation.  ## 2. Problem Statement  Parameter semantics can currently only be explained as free-form prose in an ad hoc `# Arguments` Markdown section of the item's doc comment. Such prose is not associated with any parameter by the compiler or by rustdoc, cannot be validated for coverage or staleness, cannot be located by readers or tooling at the point of use, and is not represented in rustdoc's machine-readable output.  ## 3. Scope  **In scope:** value parameters, pattern parameters, and the `self` receiver of functions, inherent and trait methods, trait implementations, and `extern` declarations; rendering in rustdoc HTML and rustdoc JSON; related lints and documentation.  **Extended scope (should):** generic type parameters, lifetime parameters, and const generic parameters.  **Out of scope:** documentation of closure parameters, fn-pointer-type parameters, tuple struct/variant fields, and non-Rust documentation pipelines.  ## 4. Functional Requirements  **FR-1 — Authoring syntax.** Doc comments (`///`, `/** … */`) and equivalent `#[doc = "…"]` attributes written immediately before a parameter in a callable's signature shall be parsed by the compiler and attached to that parameter. The construct shall no longer be rejected with an error, and shall not be silently discarded or treated as an unused doc comment.  **FR-2 — Coverage.** FR-1 shall apply to free functions, inherent methods, trait methods, trait implementation methods, and foreign (`extern`) functions, including `async`, `unsafe`, `const`, and `extern "ABI"` variants, and to the `self` receiver where a receiver is written.  **FR-3 — Compilation neutrality.** Parameter documentation shall have no effect on name resolution, type checking, lowering, MIR, or code generation. Well-formed input shall not produce new compiler errors or warnings.  **FR-4 — HTML rendering.** Rustdoc shall render per-parameter documentation on the item page, associated with the corresponding parameter of the rendered signature, using the same Markdown pipeline as item documentation. Each rendered parameter shall expose a stable, linkable anchor so that a specific parameter's documentation can be referenced in a URL.  **FR-5 — Non-identifier parameters.** Documentation shall be accepted and rendered for parameters whose pattern does not supply a simple identifier (including `_`, tuple patterns, and destructuring patterns); where no name is rendered, the documentation shall still be reachable and attributable to the correct positional parameter.  **FR-6 — JSON output.** Rustdoc JSON shall carry per-parameter documentation in the representation of the corresponding argument. Any schema change shall follow the rustdoc JSON format's existing versioning and stability policy.  **FR-7 — Markdown and linking.** Parameter documentation shall support the Markdown feature set available to item documentation, including intra-doc links to types, traits, and functions, preformatted blocks, and HTML passthrough.  **FR-8 — Doctests.** Content in parameter documentation shall not generate doctests.  **FR-9 — Lints.** The behavior of `missing_docs` shall be unchanged by default. An allow-by-default rustdoc lint shall be provided to warn when a parameter is undocumented. `unused_doc_comments` shall not fire for parameter documentation.  **FR-10 — Extended scope.** Type parameters, lifetime parameters, and const generic parameters shall be documentable and renderable by the same mechanism.  **FR-11 — Documentation.** The accepted syntax shall be specified in the Rust Reference, and rendering, JSON representation, and lint behavior shall be documented in the rustdoc book.  ## 5. Non-Functional Requirements  - **Performance:** Compilation time and rustdoc time for crates with large public APIs shall show no measurable regression attributable to the feature. - **Compatibility:** Since the construct was previously a hard error, no currently compiling source code shall change behavior. - **Cross-crate propagation:** Parameter documentation on `pub` items shall be available to downstream crates through metadata and rendered in rustdoc for dependents, subject to `#[doc(hidden)]` and `--document-private-items` handling consistent with existing item documentation.  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria  1. A documented parameter compiles without error and its documentation appears in rustdoc HTML adjacent to that parameter. 2. Every rendered parameter exposes a distinct, stable anchor that resolves to the parameter's documentation. 3. The documentation appears in rustdoc JSON at the correct positional argument, under the versioned schema. 4. Intra-doc links inside parameter documentation resolve, and broken links are reported by `rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links`. 5. Parameter documentation produces no doctests and no `unused_doc_comments` warnings. 6. The opt-in parameter-documentation lint fires for undocumented parameters and is silent by default. 7. Trait methods, trait impl methods, foreign functions, and `async`/`unsafe`/`const` items behave as specified in FR-2. 8. A documented parameter on a `pub` item is rendered in a dependent crate's documentation. 9. Output for an undocumented parameter on an otherwise unchanged item is byte-identical to the pre-change output.  ## 7. Assumptions and Dependencies  - The exact spelling of the lint name and of the rendered parameter anchor scheme is fixed at implementation time and recorded in the rustdoc book. - Implementation depends on the parameter representation in rustc's HIR/AST retaining attached documentation attributes through to rustdoc's `clean` model and to metadata encoding.
explanation: The requirement is detailed and precise about the needed per-parameter documentation feature, with clear functional and acceptance criteria, making it highly verifiable and singular. Minor ambiguities remain around exact syntax and anchor naming, preventing a perfect score for unambiguity.

requirement: # Software Requirement: Variadic Function Support in GDScript  ## Summary  GDScript shall support user-defined variadic functions that accept a variable number of arguments at call time. The language shall provide defined syntax for declaring a variadic parameter and a defined mechanism for accessing surplus arguments within the function body.  ## Motivation  GDScript functions currently have fixed arity, modifiable only by default parameter values. Developers requiring variable arguments must rely on workarounds such as explicit `Array`/`Dictionary` parameters or `callv()`. First-class variadic support improves ergonomics, readability, and interoperability for wrapper, forwarding, logging, and utility APIs.  ## Functional Requirements  1. **Declaration syntax.** The language shall provide syntax to declare that a function accepts additional arguments beyond its named parameters. All surplus arguments shall be captured into a single ordered container accessible within the function body.  2. **Access to variadic arguments.** Inside a variadic function, the captured surplus arguments shall be accessible as an ordered, indexable collection that preserves call order.  3. **Minimum arity.** A variadic function may declare zero or more leading named parameters; only arguments beyond those named parameters are collected as variadic. Required named parameters shall be validated under existing rules.  4. **Call semantics.** A variadic function shall be callable with any number of extra arguments, including zero. Extra arguments shall be appended to the variadic collection in call order.  5. **Type support.** The variadic collection may be untyped or typed. If a type is declared, each surplus argument shall be validated/converted under existing parameter type rules, producing runtime errors consistent with current typed-parameter behavior.  6. **Interaction with default parameters.** Default values shall continue to apply to named parameters preceding the variadic parameter. The variadic parameter shall not require a default value.  7. **Forwarding / spreading.** The language shall provide a defined means to forward or expand a variadic collection into another callable's argument list (or document the supported alternative) so that transparent wrapper functions can be written without loss or reordering.  8. **Uniform callable behavior.** Variadic functions shall be invocable through all existing call paths—direct calls, `call()`/`callv()`, callables, signals, and reflection—with consistent behavior.  9. **Introspection.** Variadic functions shall report their variadic nature through the reflection/metadata APIs so that tooling and bindings can detect them.  10. **Lambdas and signals.** Variadic syntax shall be usable with lambdas and signal callback handlers wherever function syntax is permitted, with behavior consistent with named functions.  11. **Built-in interoperability.** The runtime shall expose a documented mechanism for built-in/native methods to declare variadic parameter behavior consistent with script-level variadic functions.  12. **Editor support.** The editor shall provide syntax highlighting, autocompletion, and inline documentation for variadic declarations and calls.  13. **Documentation.** User-facing documentation and examples shall be provided.  ## Error Handling  - Declaring more than one variadic parameter shall be a parse/compile error. - Placing the variadic parameter anywhere other than the final position shall be a parse error. - Passing arguments that violate a declared variadic type shall raise a runtime error consistent with existing typed-parameter errors. - Misuse of the forwarding/spread construct shall produce clear compile or runtime diagnostics.  ## Non-Functional Requirements  - No measurable regression in call performance for non-variadic functions. - Variadic calls shall have performance overhead comparable to existing dynamic-argument mechanisms. - The feature shall be backward compatible; existing scripts shall continue to parse and run unchanged. - Implementation shall not break existing method binding, reflection, or GDExtension interoperability.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - A function declared with named parameters plus a variadic parameter can be called with zero, one, or many surplus arguments and receives the expected values. - A wrapper function can forward its variadic arguments to another function without loss or reordering. - Typed variadic parameters raise the expected runtime error on invalid argument types. - Static analysis and editor tooling recognize variadic declarations. - Behavior is covered by automated tests and documented.  ## Out of Scope  - Overload resolution based on variadic arity. - Named or keyword argument support.
