requirement: **Requirement: Rendering Compositor**  **ID:** REQ-RC-001 **Type:** Feature **Priority:** Should Have (unless designated otherwise by maintainers)  **Summary** The system shall provide a Rendering Compositor that combines multiple independently produced visual layers (surfaces) into a single output frame, in a defined z-order, with per-layer transforms, opacity, and blending, and presents that frame to a display or render target.  **Description** The Rendering Compositor acts as the final stage of the rendering pipeline. Each producer (window, widget, canvas, video source, or other renderer) submits its output as a layer. The compositor manages the layer tree, computes the final composition each frame, and outputs the result without requiring producers to render directly into the shared target.  **Functional Requirements**  - **FR-1 Layer management:** The compositor shall allow clients to create, update, reorder, show, hide, and destroy layers. Each layer shall have a unique identifier. - **FR-2 Z-ordering:** The compositor shall composite layers in a deterministic back-to-front order defined by their z-index. Layers with equal z-index shall be ordered by creation sequence. - **FR-3 Geometry and transforms:** Each layer shall support position, size, and an affine transform (at minimum translation, scaling, and rotation by 90° increments). - **FR-4 Opacity and blending:** Each layer shall support a global opacity value in the range [0.0, 1.0]. The compositor shall support at least source-over alpha blending and a premultiplied-alpha pipeline. - **FR-5 Clipping:** Each layer shall support a rectangular clip region. Content outside the clip region and outside the render target shall not be drawn. - **FR-6 Damage tracking:** The compositor shall track damaged regions per layer and recompose only the affected areas when possible. A full-frame recomposition shall be performed when damage cannot be determined. - **FR-7 Buffer submission:** The compositor shall accept pixel buffers from clients through a defined interface, supporting at least one common pixel format (e.g., ARGB8888 or RGBA8888). Buffers shall be reference-counted or otherwise protected so they are not released while in use by the compositor. - **FR-8 Frame scheduling:** The compositor shall produce frames at the rate of the target display's refresh cycle, or at a configurable fixed rate when no display timing is available. It shall skip composition when no damage exists. - **FR-9 Output targets:** The compositor shall present output to at least one render target (e.g., an on-screen framebuffer or an offscreen buffer). Offscreen output shall be readable by the caller. - **FR-10 Error handling:** Invalid operations (unknown layer ID, unsupported format, zero-size buffer) shall return a defined error code or raise a documented exception without crashing the compositor. Failed buffer uploads shall leave the previous frame content intact.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  - **NFR-1 Performance:** Composing a frame of up to 32 layers at 1920×1080 shall complete within 8 ms on the reference hardware defined by the project's test suite, excluding client rendering time. - **NFR-2 Thread safety:** Layer and buffer submission APIs shall be safe to call from a thread other than the composition thread. Composition shall occur on a single dedicated thread or queue. - **NFR-3 Portability:** The core compositing logic shall not depend on a specific windowing system or GPU API. Platform-specific output shall be isolated behind a backend interface. - **NFR-4 Memory:** The compositor shall not allocate new buffers per frame in steady state; intermediate buffers shall be pooled and reused. - **NFR-5 Observability:** The compositor shall expose frame timing, number of composited layers, and damaged-area statistics through a debug interface or logging at a configurable verbosity level. - **NFR-6 Compatibility:** Existing public rendering APIs shall remain source-compatible. Any new public API shall be documented in the project's API reference.  **Out of Scope (for this requirement)**  - Window management and input routing - Hardware video decode - Color management beyond sRGB - HDR tone mapping  **Acceptance Criteria**  1. A test scene with five overlapping layers of differing z-index, opacity (0.5 on at least one), and clip regions produces pixel-exact output matching a reference image within a tolerance of ±1 per channel. 2. Moving one layer by a single pixel triggers recomposition only of the union of its old and new bounds (verified via damage statistics). 3. Destroying a layer while the compositor is reading its buffer does not cause a crash or use-after-free (verified under a thread sanitizer). 4. Submitting an invalid buffer returns the documented error and the previous frame remains presented. 5. Steady-state composition of 100 consecutive frames performs zero heap allocations for intermediate buffers (verified via allocation counter). 6. The public API is documented, and all new functions have unit tests with at least 80% line coverage of the compositor module.

requirement: ## Feature Requirement: Regular Expression Support for Test Filters  ### Summary Test filters currently support only simple matching (exact names, literal substrings, and glob-like patterns). Users need the ability to select tests using regular expressions, so that large suites can be narrowed by patterns that literal matching cannot express (e.g., `^Suite::.*_smoke$`, `.*[Ff]laky.*`, alternation across several test names).  ### Motivation Selecting a subset of tests by pattern is a core daily workflow. Without regex, users must resort to multiple filters, broad literals that over-select, or external scripting. Regex support makes test selection expressive and precise, and reduces the number of filters needed for a single run.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **Filter syntax**    - Each filter option that currently accepts a literal or glob pattern (e.g. test name, file path, tag/label) must additionally accept a regular expression.    - A filter is interpreted as a regex when it is explicitly marked as such (e.g. a dedicated `regex:` prefix or a separate `--filter-regex` style option). Literal/glob behavior must remain the default so existing configurations are unaffected.  2. **Matching semantics**    - Regex matching is applied against the full identifying string of the test (e.g. the fully qualified test name, including suite/class and file path components as defined by the existing filter contract).    - Matching shall be unanchored by default: a pattern matches if it is found anywhere in the target string. Users shall be able to anchor explicitly with `^` and `$`.    - Case sensitivity shall be configurable; the default must match the behavior of existing filters (case-sensitive unless the existing option already provides a case-insensitive mode).  3. **Engine and portability**    - Use the standard regular expression syntax of the host language/runtime, and document the exact flavor supported (e.g. PCRE, ECMAScript, POSIX ERE, Go RE2), including which constructs are unsupported.    - The chosen engine must be a linear-time engine (no catastrophic backtracking) so that pathological user patterns cannot hang the test runner.  4. **Combination with existing filters**    - Regex filters must compose with all existing filter types using the same precedence and conjunctive/disjunctive rules that literal filters use today.    - Multiple regex filters of the same type must be OR-ed together (a test matching any one is selected), consistent with current multi-value filter semantics.  5. **Error handling and validation**    - An invalid regular expression must be detected before the test run starts and must produce a clear error message identifying the offending pattern, the reason it is invalid, and the filter/option that supplied it.    - An invalid regex must cause the run to fail fast with a non-zero exit status rather than silently matching nothing or aborting mid-run.  6. **Reporting**    - The run output must report how many tests were selected by each filter and the total selected, so users can confirm their pattern behaves as expected.    - When a filter selects zero tests, the existing "no tests matched" behavior must be preserved (including any configured failure or warning policy).  7. **Documentation**    - Document regex filter syntax, the supported regex flavor, matching semantics, examples, and precedence relative to other filter options.    - Provide at least one worked example showing a literal filter and its equivalent regex filter.  ### Non-Goals - Adding new filter target types (e.g. filtering on test duration or runtime output) beyond enabling regex on existing targets. - Supporting regex in assertion or matcher expressions.  ### Acceptance Criteria - A user can select tests with a pattern such as `^integration::api::.*_test$` using only filter configuration, with no source-code changes. - A pattern that matches nothing yields the documented zero-match behavior and message. - An invalid pattern (e.g. `*[`) is rejected at startup with an actionable error message and a non-zero exit code. - Existing configurations and scripts that use literal/glob filters continue to produce identical results. - Automated tests cover: valid match, no match, anchored and unanchored patterns, case-insensitive mode, multiple regex filters, invalid pattern handling, and precedence when regex and literal filters are combined.

requirement: **Requirement: Runtime Test Skipping**  The test framework shall allow a test to be marked as skipped while it is executing, based on conditions evaluated at runtime, without requiring the skip decision to be declared statically in the test's source code or configuration.  **Functional Requirements**  1. The framework shall provide an API that a test or its setup/fixture code can call during execution to skip the current test, with an optional human-readable reason. 2. A runtime skip shall immediately stop execution of the current test body. Code after the skip call shall not execute. 3. Setup and teardown hooks shall be able to trigger a runtime skip for the test they belong to. 4. A test skipped at runtime shall be reported with status "skipped," distinct from "passed," "failed," and "errored," and the reason shall appear in the report output. 5. A runtime skip shall not mark the overall test run as failed, unless the project's configuration explicitly treats skips as failures. 6. Runtime skips shall work with the framework's existing parallel execution, retry, and reporting features without altering their behavior for other tests. 7. Skipped tests shall still run their teardown or cleanup logic that the framework normally guarantees for skipped tests.  **Non-Functional Requirements**  8. The skip API shall be available in all languages and runners that the framework officially supports, with consistent naming and semantics across them. 9. Documentation shall include at least one example of conditional skipping based on an environment variable or runtime check.  **Acceptance Criteria**  - Given a test that calls the skip API with a reason, when the test runs, then the test is reported as skipped with that reason and no assertions after the call are executed. - Given a test that calls the skip API in a fixture, when the fixture runs, then the associated test is reported as skipped and its body is not executed. - Given a run in which one or more tests are skipped at runtime and none fail, when the run completes, then the exit status indicates success by default. - Given the configuration option that treats skips as failures is enabled, when a test is skipped at runtime, then the run is reported as failed.
explanation: The requirement is clearly worded with detailed functional and acceptance criteria, making it unambiguous and easily verifiable. However, it bundles multiple distinct capabilities (API, skip handling, reporting, configuration, cross-language support) rather than focusing on a single feature, reducing its singularity.

requirement: **REQ-GDSCRIPT-UNION-001: Union Type Support in Statically Typed GDScript**  **Overview** Implement union types in Typed GDScript to enable variables, function parameters, return values, and class members to accept values from a discrete set of distinct types, maintaining compile-time type safety while increasing type flexibility.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Syntax Specification**    - Support pipe-separated union syntax in type annotations: `TypeA | TypeB [| TypeC ...]`    - Applicable in: variable declarations (`var x: int | String`), function parameters (`func f(a: Node | Resource) -> void`), return types (`func g() -> int | String`), constants, signal declarations, and generic type arguments (`Array[int | String]`)    - Disambiguate from bitwise OR operator based on syntactic context (type position vs. expression position)  2. **Static Type Checking**    - Validate that assigned values are assignable to at least one member of the union    - Enforce compatibility checking against the existing type hierarchy (e.g., reject `int | Array` if they have no common supertype that makes sense, but allow `Node | Resource`)    - Support nested and chained unions: `int | String | Array[float]`    - Ensure interoperability with `Variant` (treated as union of all types)  3. **Type Narrowing and Control Flow Analysis**    - Narrow union types within conditional branches after type checks (e.g., after `if x is int:`, variable `x` is treated as `int` within that block)    - Support narrowing via `is` operator, `assert`, and pattern matching constructs    - Maintain narrowed types through local variable assignments within the same scope  4. **Member Access Rules**    - Permit direct access only to members/methods present in the intersection of all union members' interfaces (common members)    - Require explicit type narrowing before accessing type-specific members not present in all union constituents    - Provide clear compile-time error messages when accessing invalid members on un-narrowed unions  5. **Type Inference**    - Infer union types from conditional expressions: `value if condition else other_value` where types differ    - Infer appropriate union types for array/dictionary literals with heterogeneous element types where context permits  6. **Editor and Runtime Integration**    - Support `@export` on union-typed variables, displaying appropriately in the Godot inspector (may require hint strings or metadata for ambiguous unions)    - Support union types in signal parameter declarations    - Zero runtime overhead; type information erased at compile time consistent with existing static typing behavior  7. **Nullability**    - Support explicit nullable unions via `Type | null` syntax (or equivalent), ensuring `null` is treated as a valid union member when declared  **Constraints and Compatibility** - Must remain 100% backward compatible with existing GDScript code - Must function correctly in both static and dynamic typing modes (with static checks enforced only in typed contexts) - Must not degrade static analysis performance for non-union code - Parser must correctly distinguish union type syntax from bitwise OR expressions  **Acceptance Criteria** - [ ] Compiler accepts union type annotations in all specified syntactic positions without parse errors - [ ] Static analyzer rejects assignments to union variables that match no union member - [ ] Static analyzer accepts assignments matching any single union member - [ ] Type narrowing correctly restricts available members in conditional branches - [ ] Member access violations on un-narrowed unions produce compile-time errors with actionable messages - [ ] Exported union variables appear and function correctly in the Godot editor inspector - [ ] Generic types containing unions (e.g., `Array[int | String]`) enforce element type constraints - [ ] Existing test suite passes with no regressions in type checking behavior
explanation: The requirement is largely clear and includes concrete, testable acceptance criteria, though a few phrases (e.g., "makes sense" for type compatibility) introduce minor ambiguity. It defines a single feature (union type support) but enumerates many separate functional requirements, so it is not a singular statement.

requirement: ## Requirement: Exclude statically unreachable code from test coverage  The test coverage tooling must use conservative static control-flow analysis to identify executable statements and branches that are provably unreachable and exclude them from coverage metrics and reports.  ### Acceptance criteria  - Unreachable lines must be classified as excluded rather than missing and must not reduce statement or branch coverage percentages. - Provably unreachable branches must be omitted from branch totals. - Reachable but untested code must continue to be reported as missing. - Detection must cover common patterns, including code after unconditional `return`, `raise`, `break`, or `continue`, and branches controlled by compile-time constant conditions. - Dynamic conditions that cannot be proven unreachable must remain included. - Analysis must not execute application code, alter program behavior, or introduce runtime side effects. - All coverage report formats and programmatic coverage results must apply the same exclusions consistently. - Automated tests must verify exclusion behavior, percentage calculations, and conservative handling of potentially reachable code.
explanation: The requirement clearly defines the goal of excluding statically unreachable code from coverage using conservative static analysis, with concrete acceptance criteria that make the expected behavior unambiguous. It is fully verifiable through coverage reports, metrics, and automated tests that can check excluded vs missing classifications and percentage calculations. requirement: **REQ-OTA-001: Out-of-Band Code and Asset Hot Updates**  **Description:** The system shall allow application developers to publish JavaScript bundles, native-independent code, and static assets as updates that client applications download and apply without a full app store release, in accordance with the rules below.  **Scope:** - Applies to updates that do not change native binaries, native dependencies, or native permissions. - Updates that require native changes are out of scope and must be delivered through the standard store release process.  **Functional Requirements:**  1. **Update Publication**    1.1. Developers shall be able to publish an update to a named deployment channel (for example, Staging or Production) using a CLI or API.    1.2. Each update shall include a unique identifier, a version label, a content hash, a target binary version range, and a release timestamp.    1.3. Developers shall be able to roll back a deployment to a previous update with a single command or API call.  2. **Update Delivery**    2.1. The client shall check for available updates on app launch and at a configurable interval while the app is in the foreground.    2.2. The client shall download updates in the background and shall not block the UI thread during download.    2.3. The client shall verify the content hash and digital signature of every downloaded update before applying it. Updates that fail verification shall be discarded and the failure reported.    2.4. Downloads shall resume after network interruption without re-downloading previously received bytes.  3. **Update Application**    3.1. The client shall apply a downloaded update on the next cold start by default, and shall support an immediate-restart option controlled by the developer.    3.2. The client shall retain the last known-good bundle and automatically revert to it if the new update fails to launch successfully within a configurable number of attempts (default: 2).    3.3. The client shall report the outcome of each update application (success, rollback, or failure) to the update server.  4. **Targeting and Rollout**    4.1. Developers shall be able to target updates by binary version, platform (iOS, Android), device attributes, and deployment channel.    4.2. Developers shall be able to perform a staged (percentage-based) rollout and halt or expand it at any time.    4.3. Client assignment to a rollout percentage shall be deterministic per device, so a device remains in the same cohort across checks.  5. **Security**    5.1. All update transport shall use TLS 1.2 or higher.    5.2. Update packages shall be cryptographically signed with a developer-held private key; the client shall verify signatures against a bundled public key.    5.3. The system shall not permit updates to modify or bypass platform security mechanisms or store review policies beyond those permitted by the platform vendor.  6. **Observability**    6.1. The system shall provide per-update metrics: download count, install success rate, rollback rate, and active adoption by version.    6.2. Metrics shall be available within 15 minutes of client-reported events.  7. **Offline and Failure Behavior**    7.1. The application shall launch successfully using the last installed bundle when the update server is unreachable.    7.2. A failed or interrupted update check shall not degrade application functionality.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** - NFR-1: Update check and download overhead shall not add more than 500 ms to cold start time when no update is available. - NFR-2: The client SDK shall remain under 200 KB added to the app package size (excluding bundles). - NFR-3: The update service shall support at least 99.9% monthly availability for update delivery endpoints. - NFR-4: Update bundles shall be compressed in transit, with a maximum payload size configurable by the developer (default: 50 MB).  **Acceptance Criteria:** - AC-1: A developer publishes an update to Staging; a test device on the matching binary version receives, verifies, and applies it on the next cold start without a store release. - AC-2: An update with an altered byte fails signature verification, is not applied, and a failure event is recorded. - AC-3: An update that crashes on launch triggers automatic rollback to the prior bundle after the configured attempt threshold, and a rollback event is recorded. - AC-4: A 10% staged rollout delivers the update to approximately 10% of test devices, and the same devices remain in the cohort on subsequent checks. - AC-5: A rollback command restores the prior update for all devices on the next check. - AC-6: With the update server unreachable, the app launches using the last installed bundle.
explanation: The requirement is detailed and mostly unambiguous with clear, measurable verification points, but it bundles many distinct capabilities and constraints, so it is not singular.

requirement: **Requirement: General-Purpose Swarm/Mob/Flock Entity Management System**  **Summary** The system shall provide a built-in swarm management system that enables users to create, configure, simulate, and render large collections of entities (e.g., flocks, mobs, swarms, crowds) that exhibit collective behavior, while maintaining stable performance at high entity counts.  **Functional Requirements**  1. **Group Creation and Lifecycle**    - 1.1 The system shall allow a swarm group of configurable size to be instantiated via a single API call and/or editor node.    - 1.2 The system shall support adding and removing individual entities from a group at runtime without full group re-initialization.    - 1.3 The system shall support configurable spawn distributions (e.g., random volume, sphere, ring, user-defined region).  2. **Collective Behavior**    - 2.1 The system shall implement boids-style flocking (separation, alignment, cohesion) with per-group tunable weights and influence radii.    - 2.2 The system shall support, at minimum, three behavior modes selectable at runtime: Flock (boids), Mob (crowd flow toward a target), and Swarm (attraction to a moving leader or goal point).    - 2.3 The system shall expose per-group parameters (max speed, max acceleration, neighbor radius, goal/target, behavior weights) modifiable at runtime.    - 2.4 The system shall support goal-seeking and obstacle avoidance.    - 2.5 The system shall allow custom per-group or per-entity behavior to be supplied via user-defined scripts or extension points.  3. **Scale and Performance**    - 3.1 The system shall use spatial partitioning (e.g., a spatial hash grid) for neighbor queries instead of brute-force pairwise checks.    - 3.2 The system shall render entities using instanced/batched rendering to minimize draw calls.    - 3.3 The system shall provide a level-of-detail mechanism that reduces simulation fidelity (neighbor sample count, update frequency) for distant or off-screen groups.    - 3.4 The system shall support a configurable per-group simulation update rate and fixed or variable timestep integration.    - 3.5 The system shall support simulation on a background thread or compute/GPU path where available, without requiring changes to user code.  4. **Integration and Queryability**    - 4.1 The system shall integrate with the engine's existing scene graph/entity system and expose group and per-entity transforms.    - 4.2 The system shall allow external systems (raycasting, collision, AI targeting) to query the current position and state of individual entities.    - 4.3 The system shall be configurable both programmatically and through the editor/UI, where one exists.  **Non-Functional Requirements**    - NFR-1 Simulating and rendering 10,000 entities shall sustain ≥ 60 FPS on reference mid-range hardware, with the simulation step costing ≤ 5 ms per frame.    - NFR-2 Adding or removing up to 10% of a group's entities in a single frame shall not produce a frame-time spike exceeding 2 ms.    - NFR-3 Memory usage shall scale linearly with entity count and not exceed 1 KB per entity.    - NFR-4 Identical inputs, parameters, and seed shall produce identical simulation results across runs (deterministic mode).  **Acceptance Criteria**    - AC-1 A demo scene containing 10,000 flocking entities meets the performance targets in NFR-1.    - AC-2 Behavior modes can be switched at runtime without reloading the scene.    - AC-3 Groups can be created, resized, and destroyed at runtime with no frame spikes beyond NFR-2.    - AC-4 Per-entity positions returned by queries match rendered entity positions within a defined tolerance (e.g., one frame of interpolation).  **Out of Scope**    - Navigation-mesh pathfinding, skeletal animation of agents, and rigid-body-level collision response for individual swarm entities.
explanation: The requirement is detailed, measurable, and includes clear functional, non‑functional, and acceptance criteria, making it highly unambiguous and easily verifiable. It covers multiple distinct capabilities (creation, behavior, performance, integration), which slightly reduces its singularity despite being focused on a single swarm management system.

requirement: ## Requirement: TCP Keepalive Socket Option for `TcpStream`  **ID:** LIBS-TCPSTREAM-KEEPALIVE **Component:** `std::net::TcpStream` (standard library) **Type:** Functional — new public API  ### Summary Provide getter and setter methods on `TcpStream` to query, enable, configure, and disable TCP keepalive probes, without requiring platform-specific code or external crates.  ### Functional Requirements  1. **API surface** — `TcpStream` shall expose:    - `fn keepalive(&self) -> io::Result<Option<Duration>>`    - `fn set_keepalive(&self, keepalive: Option<Duration>) -> io::Result<()>`  2. **Setter semantics** — `set_keepalive` shall:    - With `Some(d)` where `d > Duration::ZERO`: enable `SO_KEEPALIVE` and set the keepalive idle time (interval before the first probe) to `d`.    - With `None`: disable TCP keepalive on the socket.    - With `Some(Duration::ZERO)`: return an `io::Error` of kind `InvalidInput` and leave the socket's existing keepalive configuration unchanged.    - With a duration exceeding the platform's representable limit: return an `io::Error` of kind `InvalidInput` rather than silently truncating.  3. **Getter semantics** — `keepalive` shall return:    - `Ok(Some(d))` with the currently configured idle time when keepalive is enabled.    - `Ok(None)` when keepalive is disabled.  4. **Round-trip consistency** — calling `keepalive()` immediately after a successful `set_keepalive(Some(d))` shall return `Ok(Some(d))` on platforms that support reading the option.  5. **Platform mapping** — implementations shall use `TCP_KEEPIDLE` (Linux/Android), `TCP_KEEPALIVE` (macOS/iOS/other BSDs), or `SIO_KEEPALIVE_VALS` (Windows, with the system-default probe interval/count). On platforms where setting or querying the idle time is unsupported, the corresponding method shall return an `io::Error` instead of silently ignoring the request, and this behavior shall be documented.  6. **Failure isolation** — if any step of the setter fails, the method shall return the resulting `io::Error`; the resulting socket state on partial failure shall be documented.  7. **Documentation** — doc comments shall follow the style of `set_nodelay`/`nodelay`, including examples, error conditions, and platform-specific notes.  ### Non-Goals Configuring the keepalive probe interval (`TCP_KEEPINTVL`) or probe count (`TCP_KEEPCNT`) is out of scope and may be addressed by a follow-up requirement.  ### Acceptance Criteria - Both methods compile with the specified signatures as an additive, semver-compatible change. - Automated tests on supported platforms verify: enabling with a positive duration, disabling via `None`, zero-duration rejection with `InvalidInput`, and getter/setter round-trip. - Tests for unsupported platforms are conditionally compiled/gated accordingly. - Documentation renders with examples and platform notes and passes review.

requirement: **Requirement: Platform-Independent Path Types**  The library shall provide the types `UnixPath` and `WindowsPath`, along with their owned counterparts `UnixPathBuf` and `WindowsPathBuf` (mirroring `Path` and `PathBuf`), on all supported target platforms, regardless of the host operating system.  1. **Universal availability:** All four types shall be compiled and usable on Unix, Windows, and any other supported platform without conditional compilation (`#[cfg]`) or feature gating required by the consumer. 2. **Consistent API:** `UnixPath`/`UnixPathBuf` shall implement the same method surface and trait implementations as `Path`/`PathBuf` (e.g., component iteration, `join`, `parent`, `file_name`, `extension`, `with_extension`, `starts_with`, `strip_prefix`), with semantics defined by Unix path conventions. `WindowsPath`/`WindowsPathBuf` shall provide the equivalent API with semantics defined by Windows path conventions, including drive prefixes, UNC paths, and both `\` and `/` separators. 3. **Convention-correct parsing:** Parsing and component decomposition shall follow the rules of the named convention irrespective of the host platform. For example, `WindowsPath` shall treat `C:\foo` as having a prefix, and `UnixPath` shall treat `\` as a valid filename character. 4. **Native interoperability:** Conversions between `UnixPath`/`WindowsPath` and the native `Path`/`PathBuf` shall be provided where the conversion is meaningful, and any lossy or invalid conversion shall return an error or `Option` rather than panic or silently alter the path. 5. **Trait support:** All types shall implement `Clone`, `Debug`, `Eq`, `Ord`, `Hash`, `AsRef<...>`, `Borrow` (for the owned/borrowed pairs), `Display` where applicable, and `serde` serialization behind an existing or new optional feature flag. 6. **No I/O on foreign paths:** Filesystem operations (e.g., `exists`, `metadata`, `read_dir`) shall not be exposed on `UnixPath` or `WindowsPath` unless the host platform matches the path's convention, to avoid silently operating on the wrong filesystem. 7. **Documentation and tests:** Each type shall be documented with its parsing rules and include unit tests that run on every platform in CI, verifying convention-specific behavior independently of the host OS.

requirement: **Requirement ID:** REQ-RC-001 **Title:** Rendering Compositor Module  **Description:** Implement a modular rendering compositor that orchestrates the combination of multiple visual layers, intermediate render targets, and post-processing effects into a unified final frame output, supporting both 2D and 3D rendering pipelines.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. **Layer Management:** The system shall support dynamic creation, reordering, and removal of render layers at runtime, with each layer having configurable z-index/priority, opacity (0.0–1.0), and visibility state. 2. **Compositing Operations:** The compositor shall implement standard blend modes (Normal/Alpha, Additive, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Subtract) selectable per layer, with support for custom shader-based blending when required. 3. **Render Target Chaining:** The system shall allow intermediate render targets (textures/framebuffers) to be bound as input sources for subsequent layers, enabling multi-pass rendering workflows. 4. **Clipping and Scissoring:** Each layer shall support rectangular viewport clipping and scissor testing to limit rendering to specific screen regions, optimizing GPU fill-rate usage. 5. **Post-Processing Pipeline:** The compositor shall provide hooks for inserting shader-based post-processing effects (e.g., bloom, blur, color grading, tone mapping) at defined stages: pre-composite (per layer) or post-composite (final output). 6. **Resolution Scaling:** Support per-layer resolution scaling factors with automatic bilinear or bicubic upscaling/downscaling to match the final output resolution.  **Non-Functional Requirements:** - **Performance:** Compositing overhead shall not exceed 0.5 milliseconds per frame at 1920×1080 resolution on reference hardware (mid-tier GPU). - **Memory Management:** Render target buffers shall be pooled and reused across frames to prevent GPU memory allocation churn; total VRAM usage shall not exceed 2× the sum of active layer buffer sizes. - **Thread Safety:** The compositor scene graph shall be immutable during the render phase; layer modifications shall be permitted only during a dedicated "prepare" phase before frame submission.  **Interface Requirements:** - Provide a `RenderCompositor` class/API exposing: `addLayer(config)`, `removeLayer(id)`, `setLayerOrder(id, zIndex)`, `setBlendMode(id, mode)`, `addPostProcessEffect(effect)`, and `render(commandBuffer)`. - Support both immediate-mode (command recording per frame) and retained-mode (persistent scene description) usage patterns. - Configuration of static layer hierarchies shall be loadable from declarative formats (JSON/YAML).  **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] Semi-transparent overlapping layers composite correctly according to alpha blending rules with correct occlusion ordering. - [ ] Dynamic reordering of layers updates the final image without requiring pipeline reconstruction or shader recompilation. - [ ] Post-processing effects apply to the accumulated composite of all layers below them in the pipeline, not to individual layers unless explicitly configured. - [ ] Memory profiling confirms zero memory leaks after 10,000 consecutive frame render cycles with 8 active layers. - [ ] The system supports a minimum of 4 concurrent intermediate render targets in a single compositing pass. - [ ] Scissored layers do not render pixels outside their defined clipping rectangles (verified via pixel-perfect testing).

requirement: # Requirement: Flutter Support for Apple Watch (watchOS)  **Requirement ID:** FLT-WATCHOS-001 **Type:** New platform support (major feature) **Priority:** P1 (strategic platform expansion) **Origin:** Informal feature request — "Flutter support for Apple Watch" **Affected components:** `flutter/engine` (darwin embedder), `flutter/flutter` (framework, tooling, plugins), `packages/flutter_tools`, `packages/flutter`  ---  ## 1. Background and Motivation  Flutter currently supports building for iOS, Android, web, macOS, Windows, and Linux. There is no supported way to render Flutter content inside a watchOS app, forcing watch developers to either ship native SwiftUI/WatchKit interfaces or rebuild the same UI twice (once for the phone companion app, once for the watch).  Demand exists for: - Companion watch experiences that reuse an existing Flutter codebase (e.g., fitness trackers, chat, remote controls, companion dashboards). - Consistent look-and-feel, state management, and business logic shared between the iOS phone app and the watch app. - Participation in the growing watchOS app ecosystem, including third-party Flutter plugins.  The request is therefore to make watchOS a first-class Flutter **embedding** target, on par with iOS.  ---  ## 2. Scope  ### 2.1 In Scope  | Area | Description | |---|---| | Engine embedder | A `watchos` platform embedder providing `FlutterEngine`, `FlutterViewController`, `FlutterTexture`, `FlutterPlatformView`, and the standard `FlutterPlugin` lifecycle. | | `dart:ui` | A watchOS-conditional implementation of `dart:ui` exposing the full rendering, text, image, and platform-channel surface. | | Framework | `flutter/cupertino.dart` and `flutter/widgets.dart` render correctly on watchOS; no watchOS-conditional crashes or missing intrinsics. | | Tooling | `flutter create --platforms=watchos`, `flutter build watchos`, `flutter run -d <watchOS device>`, `flutter attach`, `flutter test --platform watchos` (where applicable). | | Build output | Production and debug `.app` bundles for the watchOS app target, including a WatchKit app extension as required by watchOS packaging rules. | | Plugins | Platform channels (including `MethodChannel`, `EventChannel`, `BasicMessageChannel`), `Texture` registry, and plugin registration on watchOS. Plugins without a watchOS implementation must fail gracefully. | | Developer experience | Hot reload / hot restart against a watchOS target, DevTools integration, `flutter doctor` watchOS checks. |  ### 2.2 Out of Scope  - **Standalone watchOS apps.** watchOS apps are always companion apps embedded inside a containing iOS app. The requirement covers Flutter content inside the watchOS app/extension only; the containing iOS app is not required to be Flutter-based. - Business/UI widgets specific to watch interactions (e.g., crown rotation gestures, workout sessions, background refresh) beyond providing the platform plumbing to build them. - Distribution, App Store review, or notarization specifics beyond producing a valid, signable bundle. - Native SwiftUI/WatchKit interoperability beyond standard platform channels.  ---  ## 3. Target Platform and Constraints  - **Minimum OS:** watchOS 7.0. - **Architectures:** `arm64_32` (watchOS 7–8, Series 3 and earlier) and `arm64` (Series 4 and later). `x86_64`/`arm64` for the watchOS Simulator. - **Rendering backend:** Metal is the only supported GPU API on watchOS. The watchOS embedder must use the Metal/Impeller path; an OpenGL/ES backend is not permitted. The Skia fallback may be used only if Impeller is not yet enabled and must be documented as deprecated. - **UI framework:** No watchOS native view system is exposed; Flutter renders all content itself, consistent with the iOS embedder model. - **Bundle structure:** The watchOS app produced by Flutter must be structured so that it can be embedded in a containing iOS app's `WatchKit` app bundle as required by Xcode.  ---  ## 4. Functional Requirements  ### FR-1 — Engine / Embedder  - **FR-1.1** Provide a `darwin/watchos` platform embedder target that builds a Flutter engine library for watchOS device and simulator architectures. - **FR-1.2** Implement `FlutterEngine` for watchOS supporting: initialization with entrypoint arguments and Dart entrypoint, Dart VM flags, rendering surface creation, task runner, and lifecycle (`run`, `destroy`, `shutdown`). - **FR-1.3** Implement `FlutterViewController` for watchOS as the `WKInterfaceController`-hosted Flutter view, supporting view sizing and safe-area handling for all watch screen sizes. - **FR-1.4** Implement `FlutterTexture` and `FlutterPlatformView` registries on watchOS. - **FR-1.5** Implement the plugin lifecycle (`register(with registrar:)`, `handle(_:)`) and plugin registration mechanism for watchOS. - **FR-1.6** Expose platform channels over the watchOS embedder, including `FlutterMethodChannel`, `FlutterEventChannel`, and `FlutterBasicMessageChannel`. - **FR-1.7** Support Dart VM service and `--observatory`/DDS connection for the watchOS target so that DevTools, hot reload, and the VM service protocol function identically to other platforms. - **FR-1.8** Handle watchOS app lifecycle transitions (foreground, inactive, background) and propagate them to the Dart framework so that `AppLifecycleState` and `WidgetsBindingObserver` behave correctly. - **FR-1.9** Support background execution limits, including the system terminating the app while in the background, without data corruption.  ### FR-2 — `dart:ui` and Framework  - **FR-2.1** Provide a watchOS implementation of `dart:ui` with no unimplemented throwing members for: canvas and picture APIs, image decoding, font loading and text layout, `Color`, `Offset`, `Rect`, `Path`, `Paint`, `Shader`, `MaskFilter`, `ImageFilter`, `Clip`, `Vertices`, `Paragraph`, `ParagraphBuilder`, `Scene`, `SceneBuilder`, `Window`, and `PlatformDispatcher`. - **FR-2.2** `PlatformDispatcher` on watchOS must report the correct `devicePixelRatio`, `physicalSize`, `views`, and `padding`/`viewInsets` for each watch screen size. - **FR-2.3** `PlatformDispatcher` must expose watchOS-specific accessibility and system affordances where applicable (e.g., `accessibilityFeatures`). - **FR-2.4** `flutter/cupertino.dart` must render correctly on watchOS. `CupertinoApp`, `CupertinoPageScaffold`, `CupertinoNavigationBar`, `CupertinoButton`, `CupertinoTextField`, `CupertinoActivityIndicator`, `CupertinoSlidingSegmentedControl`, and `CupertinoTheme` must not throw. - **FR-2.5** `CupertinoThemeData` must resolve a watchOS-appropriate default text theme and font family fallbacks using watchOS system fonts; no missing-glyph or tofu rendering for standard Latin text. - **FR-2.6** The `Material` library and `WidgetsApp` must function on watchOS without platform-specific failures. - **FR-2.7** Semantics and accessibility trees must be produced on watchOS so that VoiceOver works on the watch. - **FR-2.8** Provide a `watchOS`-aware default `MediaQuery` (no system padding unless the platform reports it) and a documented `TargetPlatform.watchOS` value that `defaultTargetPlatform` returns on watchOS.  ### FR-3 — Tooling and Build  - **FR-3.1** `flutter create --platforms=watchos` must generate a watchOS project (Xcode project with a watchOS app target and WatchKit extension), and `flutter create .` in an existing Flutter project must add watchOS support. - **FR-3.2** `flutter build watchos` must produce a signed/unsigned watchOS `.app` bundle suitable for embedding in a containing iOS app, with correct Info.plist, entitlements placeholder, and architectures. - **FR-3.3** `flutter build watchos --release` and `--profile` must be supported, with AOT compilation for release/profile and JIT for debug. - **FR-3.4** `flutter run` must support deploying to and launching on a watchOS device or simulator, with hot reload and hot restart functional. - **FR-3.5** `flutter devices` must list watchOS devices and simulators with a `watchOS` platform identifier. - **FR-3.6** `flutter doctor` must report the watchOS toolchain status: Xcode version, SDK presence, CocoaPods, and provisioning/profile status, mirroring the existing iOS checks. - **FR-3.7** WatchOS deployment must be expressible via `flutter build watchos --target-platform=arm64|arm64_32` (and simulator arch) and via Xcode build settings. - **FR-3.8** Support both CocoaPods and Swift Package Manager dependency mechanisms for Flutter-based watchOS apps. - **FR-3.9** Provide a documented, supported path for a Flutter watchOS app to be embedded in a containing iOS app (project structure, bundle IDs, `WKCompanionAppBundleIdentifier`, code-signing team requirements).  ### FR-4 — Plugins  - **FR-4.1** The plugin system must allow a plugin to declare a watchOS implementation via an iOS-conditional (`watchos`) platform folder, following the existing federated-plugin pattern. - **FR-4.2** Plugin registration on watchOS must be automatic through the generated `GeneratedPluginRegistrant`, and must not break when a dependency has no watchOS implementation. - **FR-4.3** A plugin without a watchOS implementation must produce a clear, actionable error (or a documented "not supported on watchOS" exception type) rather than a crash or silent no-op. - **FR-4.4** Provide a `MissingPluginException` equivalent that identifies the watchOS platform, so plugin authors can branch on platform support.  ### FR-5 — Quality of Life  - **FR-5.1** Provide sample apps in `flutter/examples` demonstrating a Flutter watchOS companion embedded in an iOS app. - **FR-5.2** Publish official documentation covering project setup, build/run commands, plugin authoring for watchOS, platform-channel usage with native WatchKit/SwiftUI code, and known limitations. - **FR-5.3** Provide a `flutter watchos` platform entry in the platform-support matrix and in `flutter --version` / `flutter doctor -v` output.  ---  ## 5. Non-Functional Requirements  - **NFR-1 (Startup):** Cold start of a minimal Flutter watchOS app to first frame ≤ 1.5 s on an Apple Watch Series 4 (arm64) in debug, and ≤ 800 ms in release profile. - **NFR-2 (Memory):** A minimal Flutter watchOS app must not exceed 60 MB resident memory on device; the framework must not load unnecessary subsystems for the watch (e.g., full Material library rasterization caches) when unused. - **NFR-3 (Frame rate):** The renderer must sustain 60 FPS for typical scrolling/animation workloads on Series 4+ hardware, with no dropped-frame spikes above 100 ms during interaction. - **NFR-4 (Battery):** The engine must release GPU resources on `AppLifecycleState.paused`/`detached` and must not schedule continuous frame production while the watch app is backgrounded. - **NFR-5 (Battery/energy):** Idle Flutter watchOS apps must not schedule frames when there is no animation, matching the engine's existing "no frame scheduled" optimization. - **NFR-6 (Accessibility):** All Flutter-rendered content must be exposed to VoiceOver on watchOS, with correct roles, labels, and traits. - **NFR-7 (Portability):** The implementation must not regress existing iOS, Android, macOS, web, Windows, or Linux builds; CI must remain green across all supported platforms. - **NFR-8 (Code quality):** The embedder must pass the project's lint/analyzer gates, use the shared Darwin embedder infrastructure where possible, and avoid duplicating logic that can be shared with the iOS embedder. - **NFR-9 (Localization):** Date/time/number formatting must respect the watch's locale and 24-hour settings.  ---  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria  1. `flutter create --platforms=watchos my_app` succeeds and produces a runnable watchOS target. 2. `flutter build watchos --release` produces a watchOS `.app` bundle that Xcode accepts as a watchOS app target, and that runs on a physical watch and on a watchOS simulator, rendering a Flutter UI. 3. `flutter run -d <watchOS device>` attaches successfully; editing Flutter source triggers a hot reload on the watch within 2 seconds. 4. A `MethodChannel` round trip between Dart and native Swift code in the WatchKit extension completes successfully, and an `EventChannel` delivers a stream of events. 5. A plugin with a `watchos` implementation registers and its methods are invokable from Dart; a plugin without one fails with a documented, catchable "unsupported on watchOS" error rather than crashing the app. 6. `flutter doctor` reports the watchOS toolchain correctly on both macOS with Xcode installed and on a machine without it. 7. VoiceOver announces Flutter-rendered text and controls on a physical watch. 8. `PlatformDispatcher.instance.views` and `defaultTargetPlatform` return watchOS-appropriate values, and `CupertinoApp` renders with watchOS-appropriate typography without missing glyphs. 9. All existing platform CI jobs pass with no regressions. 10. Documentation and at least one example app are published.  ---  ## 7. Delivery Plan (Phased)  | Phase | Contents | Exit criteria | |---|---|---| | **Phase 0 — Foundation** | Engine `darwin/watchos` embedder skeleton; `dart:ui` watchOS target; CI build for device + simulator architectures. | Engine loads and renders an empty/clear frame on watchOS simulator. | | **Phase 1 — MVP** | `FlutterEngine` + `FlutterViewController`; platform channels; plugin lifecycle; `flutter create/build/run` for watchOS; `CupertinoApp` usable; debug mode with hot reload. | Acceptance criteria 1–4 met in debug. | | **Phase 2 — Production readiness** | Release/profile AOT; signing and embedding in a containing iOS app; perf/memory budgets; accessibility; lifecycle and background behavior. | Acceptance criteria 2, 6, 7 met in release; NFR-1–NFR-4 measured and met. | | **Phase 3 — Ecosystem** | Plugin guidance for watchOS, `MissingPluginException` semantics, DevTools parity, docs, examples, `flutter doctor` completeness. | Acceptance criteria 5, 8, 9, 10 met. |  ---  ## 8. Open Questions  1. Should watchOS reuse the existing iOS embedder sources via a shared conditional compilation layer, or be a separate embedder directory with shared components extracted? (Affects NFR-8 and long-term maintenance cost.) 2. Is the WatchKit **extension** the required host for Flutter content, or should Flutter also be able to run in the WatchKit **app** (SwiftUI host) target? The former is the conventional model; the latter is technically harder. 3. What is the desired behavior for `flutter build watchos` output that is not embedded in an iOS app — should the tool warn or error? 4. Should `flutter run` support deploying directly to a watch (via the paired iPhone) or only to a simulator/paired device through Xcode tooling? 5. Which third-party plugins are in scope for official watchOS implementations in the first release (e.g., `url_launcher`, `path_provider`, `shared_preferences`, `connectivity_plus`)? 6. Are watchOS-specific `WidgetsApp`/`CupertinoApp` defaults (e.g., a distinct back-button behavior, haptic feedback integration) required for Phase 1 or deferred to Phase 3?

requirement: ## Requirement: Customizable Project Structure (Platforms)  **Summary** The system must allow each project to declare and customize its own set of *platforms* — that is, the project structures, target layouts, and associated build/analyze steps the tool understands — instead of relying on a single hardcoded structure. Platforms should be declarable via configuration, composable with the built-in defaults, and selectable at runtime.  **User story** As a developer working on a non-standard project layout (e.g., a monorepo, embedded firmware, or a legacy directory convention), I want to define the platforms my project supports — including their directory layout, source roots, build commands, and metadata — so that all tooling (project creation, build, inspection, reporting) operates on my actual structure rather than an imposed one.  **Functional requirements** 1. **Platform declaration:** A project (and optionally a user/global scope) must be able to declare one or more platforms via a configuration file or equivalent declarative mechanism. Each platform entry defines at minimum: platform name/identifier, root path, source/output directories, and associated commands or build steps. 2. **Built-in defaults preserved:** Predefined platforms remain available out of the box and can be used unmodified; their definitions must be introspectable and documented. 3. **Extensibility:** New platforms can be added by users without modifying or recompiling the tool; third-party/platform plugins may contribute platform definitions through the same extension mechanism. 4. **Override & merge semantics:** Project-level configuration must be able to extend, override, or disable individual fields of a built-in platform. Deterministic precedence must be defined (e.g., project > user/global > built-in default) and documented. 5. **Validation:** Invalid or conflicting platform definitions (duplicate names, missing required fields, unknown paths) must be rejected with actionable error messages that identify the offending configuration source and field. 6. **Discovery & listing:** The tool must provide a way to list all platforms available to the current project, indicating which are built-in, user-defined, or project-defined, and which is currently active. 7. **Selection:** The active platform must be selectable explicitly (configuration value or command-line option) and, where a project unambiguously maps to a single platform, resolvable automatically. Resolution failures must list the available platforms. 8. **Consumption:** Project scaffolding, build, inspection, and any output/reporting steps must operate against the resolved platform's structure, so that creating a project from a custom platform produces the declared layout. 9. **Documentation:** The platform configuration schema, available fields, precedence rules, and examples must be documented alongside the existing project documentation.  **Non-functional requirements** - Configuration loading must be schema-validated and fail fast with clear diagnostics. - Platform definitions must be resolution-independent of the current working directory. - Existing projects that do not configure custom platforms must continue to behave exactly as before (backwards compatibility). - Platform resolution and execution must not introduce perceptible performance overhead for typical project sizes.

requirement: **Requirement: no_std-Compatible I/O Traits and Cursor**  The library shall provide `Read`, `Write`, and `Cursor` abstractions that are available in `no_std` builds, without depending on the `std` crate.  1. **Availability:** When the `std` feature is disabled, the crate shall expose `Read`, `Write`, and `Cursor` types with API signatures compatible with their `std::io` counterparts. 2. **No std dependency:** These types shall be implemented using only `core` and, where needed, `alloc`, and shall not require the `std` crate or an operating system. 3. **Error handling:** I/O operations shall return a custom error type usable in `no_std` environments, and it shall convert to or from `std::io::Error` when the `std` feature is enabled. 4. **Cursor behavior:** `Cursor` shall wrap in-memory buffers (such as `&[u8]`, `&mut [u8]`, and `Vec<u8>` when `alloc` is available), track a position, and implement `Read`, `Write`, and seeking semantics equivalent to `std::io::Cursor`. 5. **Feature parity:** When the `std` feature is enabled, the `no_std` types shall interoperate with the standard `std::io` traits without duplicating implementations or changing observable behavior. 6. **Testing:** The crate shall pass its I/O test suite in a `no_std` build configuration, verified by a CI target that compiles for an embedded or `no_std` target.

requirement: ## Requirement: Transformer Input Embedding Layer and Positional Encodings  ### Background The project's Transformer implementation currently processes input tokens/characters without a dedicated embedding layer and without any mechanism to encode token order. This means the model receives no learned dense representation of its inputs and, because attention is permutation-invariant over the sequence, cannot distinguish the relative or absolute position of tokens.  ### Objective Extend the Transformer implementation so that every input sequence is first converted into a sequence of dense vectors by a trainable embedding layer, and so that positional information is added to those vectors before the encoder/decoder stacks are applied.  ### Functional Requirements  **1. Token Embedding Layer** - Provide a trainable embedding lookup table that maps each token (or character) in the vocabulary index space to a dense vector of size `d_model`. - The vocabulary size and embedding dimension must be configurable at model construction time (e.g., `vocab_size`, `d_model`). - Embedding weights must be included in the model's parameter list so they are updated by the optimizer during training. - The layer must apply dropout to the embedding output, consistent with the model's existing dropout configuration.  **2. Positional Encoding** - Implement positional encoding that produces one vector of size `d_model` per sequence position and is added element-wise to the token embeddings. - Provide two selectable variants:   - **Fixed (sinusoidal) encoding**: computed from the standard sine/cosine formula, non-trainable, computed for positions `0..max_len-1` and cached for reuse across batches.   - **Learned (trainable) embedding**: a trainable lookup table of shape `(max_seq_len, d_model)`, optimized jointly with the model. - The maximum supported sequence length (`max_len` / `max_position`) must be configurable. - Positional encoding must be applied identically to the encoder input and to the decoder input (self-attention side), so that both stacks receive position-aware representations.  **3. Scale / Initialization Behaviour** - The embedding output must be scaled by `sqrt(d_model)` before positional encoding is added, so that the magnitude of the token representation and the positional component are comparable. - Embedding weights must be initialized using the project's standard parameter initialization scheme (e.g., normal with mean 0 and standard deviation `0.02`), and all newly introduced parameters must use the same scheme as existing parameters.  **4. Integration with Existing Model** - The embedding and positional encoding modules must be exposed as reusable, composable layers that can be instantiated independently of the full Transformer. - The Transformer forward path must use the embedding layer and positional encoding automatically; no caller-side pre-processing should be required. - The decoder's output projection must operate on the same `d_model` space as the embeddings, and optional weight tying between the token embedding matrix and the output projection must be supported (configurable, defaulting to disabled unless already supported elsewhere in the project). - Existing encoder/decoder attention, masking, and causal-masking behaviour must remain unchanged.  **5. API and Configuration** - Construction must accept, at minimum: `vocab_size`, `d_model`, `max_len`, a positional-encoding mode selector (`sinusoidal` | `learned`), and `dropout`. - Configuration of the same options must be possible through the project's standard configuration mechanism (config file / dataclass / CLI flags), following existing naming conventions. - Providing a `vocab_size` incompatible with the dataset's vocabulary must fail early with a clear error message.  **6. Testing** - Unit tests must verify: embedding output shape `(batch, seq_len, d_model)`; that distinct token indices produce distinct vectors; that learned positional embeddings receive gradients; that sinusoidal encodings match the reference formula; that the encoder and decoder both receive position-aware inputs; and that the full Transformer forward/backward pass runs end-to-end with the new layers enabled. - Existing tests must continue to pass without modification.  ### Non-Goals - Changes to the attention mechanism, multi-head configuration, or feed-forward block architecture. - Sub-word/byte-level tokenization changes; the embedding layer operates on whatever token index space the existing data pipeline produces. - Relative or rotary positional schemes; only absolute (sinusoidal or learned) encodings are in scope.  ### Deliverables - Implementation of the embedding and positional encoding layers plus their integration into the Transformer. - Updated configuration/API surface and documentation describing the new options. - Test coverage for the new behaviour and a passing full test suite.
explanation: The requirement is highly detailed and leaves little room for interpretation, making it unambiguous; it includes concrete, measurable criteria that can be verified via tests, giving it high verifiability; however it bundles multiple distinct functionalities (token embedding, positional encoding, scaling, integration, API, testing) rather than a single capability, resulting in low singularity.

requirement: ## Requirement: Parallel Associative Scan  ### Summary The project shall provide a reusable **parallel associative scan** primitive that computes a prefix-reduction (scan) over a sequence using any user-supplied *associative* binary operator, executed in parallel across devices (e.g. GPU) and/or CPU threads. This enables linear-time, log-depth prefix operations required by algorithms such as linear attention / state-space models (Mamba-style), cumulative sums/products, and hierarchical reductions, without the quadratic cost of naive sequential scans.  ### Functional Requirements 1. **Generic operator support**    - The scan shall accept a user-defined associative binary operator `op(a, b)` together with an optional identity element, and shall be applied element-wise over the sequence dimension.    - Operators shall be supported as: (a) C++/host callables invoked through a dispatch mechanism, and (b) device-side functors/lambdas usable within GPU kernels.    - The API shall clearly document the associativity contract (`op(op(a,b),c) == op(a,op(b,c))`) and the semantics of the identity element.  2. **Scan modes**    - **Inclusive scan:** result element `i` equals `op(x_0, ..., x_i)`.    - **Exclusive scan:** result element `i` equals `op(x_0, ..., x_{i-1})`, with the identity (or a caller-specified initial value) at index `0`.    - The mode shall be selectable at runtime or via compile-time template parameters.  3. **Parallel algorithm**    - The implementation shall use a parallel prefix (up-sweep / down-sweep, Blelloch-style) formulation with `O(log N)` depth and `O(N)` work, distributing work across available threads/blocks.    - Correctness shall not depend on the operator being commutative; operand order shall be preserved exactly.    - The implementation shall handle arbitrary sequence lengths, including lengths not a power of two, and non-contiguous/strided inputs via strides or gathered indices.  4. **Multi-dimensional / batched operation**    - The scan shall operate over a specified axis of a multi-dimensional tensor (rank ≥ 1) with arbitrary batch dimensions, without requiring the user to flatten or copy data manually.    - Dtypes/shapes/layouts shall match the framework's existing conventions so the primitive composes with existing tensor, broadcasting, and autograd facilities.  5. **Composability and integration**    - The scan shall be usable inside custom kernels (device-side) as well as from host-level eager APIs.    - It shall support use as a building block in higher-level modules (e.g. gated linear-attention / selective-scan layers), and shall compose with existing operator-registration, shape-inference, and dispatch mechanisms.    - If the project provides automatic differentiation, gradients shall be derivable for the scan (reverse-mode), or the lack thereof shall be explicitly documented.  6. **Performance requirements**    - For a sequence length of `N = 2^k` on a single modern GPU, the implementation shall achieve a speedup of at least `10×` over a sequential scan for `N ≥ 2^16`, and shall reach within `1.5×` of the memory-bandwidth-bound optimum for element-wise-add and element-wise-multiply operators.    - Occupancy and kernel-launch overhead shall be bounded; small-N calls shall use a single-block path avoiding excessive launch overhead.  ### Non-functional Requirements - **Correctness:** Results must match a reference sequential scan (bitwise for integer and floating-point associative operators) across all supported dtypes, sequence lengths (including non-power-of-two and `N = 1`), and boundary conditions (empty input, single element). - **Testability:** Unit tests shall compare parallel results against a CPU reference implementation for randomized operators, shapes, and strides; tests shall cover both inclusive and exclusive modes and multiple operators. - **Determinism:** Repeated runs with identical inputs shall produce identical outputs. - **Documentation:** Public API documentation shall state the operator contract, supported dtypes/layouts, the parallel algorithm used, and provide at least one worked example.  ### Out of Scope - Non-associative reductions (which cannot be expressed as a scan) — the API shall detect or document this limitation. - Automatic discovery or verification of associativity for arbitrary user operators. - Multi-GPU distributed scan across nodes (the scan is parallelized within a device).
explanation: The requirement is detailed and largely precise, defining the operator, scan modes, algorithm, and integration points clearly, though a few aspects (e.g., optional identity handling) could be more explicit, resulting in a high but not perfect unambiguity score. It contains concrete, measurable criteria such as bitwise correctness, specific speed‑up targets, and testability requirements, making verification straightforward. All sub‑requirements describe facets of a single parallel associative scan primitive, so the requirement is singular in focus.

requirement: Requirement: Add BLAKE3 Hash Function Support to x/crypto  1. Compatibility 4.1 The package shall follow the conventions and licensing of the golang.org/x/crypto module. 4.2 The package shall not introduce new dependencies outside the Go standard library and existing x/crypto dependencies.

requirement: # Requirement: Union Types in Typed GDScript  GDScript shall support explicit union type annotations as part of its static type system. A union declares that a value may be any one of several alternative types without introducing a runtime wrapper or coercing values between alternatives.  ## Syntax  Union members shall be separated by `|`, with optional surrounding whitespace:  ```gdscript var score: int | float = 1 var label: String | StringName = "hello" var target: Node2D | Node3D | null var values: Array[int | String] = [1, "two"]  func transform(value: int | String) -> int | String:     return value ```  - The parser shall distinguish the union operator from the bitwise OR operator by context. - Union members may be built-in types, named script classes, enums, `null`, or `Variant`. - A union shall contain at least one non-null type. - `void` shall only be valid as the sole return type and shall not be valid as a union member.  ## Supported Locations  Union annotations shall be accepted wherever GDScript currently permits an explicit type annotation, including:  - Local variables and constants - Class member variables - Function parameters - Function return types - Signal parameters - Element and value types of typed collections  Type inference shall remain unchanged: unions shall only be created through explicit annotations.  ## Type-Checking Rules  - A statically typed value shall be assignable to a union when its type is compatible with at least one union member under existing GDScript assignability and conversion rules. - A union-typed value shall be assignable to another union when every possible source alternative is assignable to at least one target alternative. - A union-typed value shall not be implicitly converted or narrowed to one alternative. - A union-typed value may be assigned to a single-type target only if that target accepts every possible union alternative, unless an existing explicit narrowing or casting mechanism applies. - Function arguments, return values, variable initializers, default parameter values, signal arguments, and assignments shall all be validated against the declared union. - `null` shall be accepted only when `null` is an explicit union member. - A union containing `Variant` shall follow existing `Variant` semantics and accept any value, including `null`. - Accessing a property, calling a method, or using an operator shall produce a compile-time error when the operation is not supported by every applicable non-null union member. A `Variant` member shall retain existing dynamic-access behavior.  ## Runtime Behavior  - Union annotations shall be compile-time constructs; the runtime value shall remain a `Variant` containing the original value and concrete type. - Assignment shall not coerce a value to another union member. For example, assigning a `String` to `int | String` shall retain the value as a `String`. - When a dynamically typed value is assigned to a union-typed variable or parameter, the runtime type shall be checked against the union members. An incompatible value shall produce a runtime error identifying the accepted alternatives. - Typed arrays and dictionaries containing union element types shall accept values matching any member and reject values matching no member.  ## Diagnostics and Tooling  - Invalid union syntax or unsupported union members shall produce a parse-time error with the source location. - Type incompatibilities shall produce a compile-time error that identifies the invalid expression and lists the accepted union alternatives. - Runtime validation failures shall identify the declared union and the received value type. - Editor type displays, hover information, generated documentation, and signatures shall render unions as their alternatives separated by `|`.  ## Acceptance Criteria  - Valid declarations such as `int | float`, `Node2D | Node3D | null`, and `Array[int | String]` compile and execute correctly. - Assigning a value incompatible with every alternative is rejected at compile time when its type is known. - Assigning an incompatible dynamically typed value is rejected at runtime. - `null` is rejected for unions that do not explicitly include `null`. - Common properties and methods remain accessible, while unsupported member access is rejected. - Existing single-type annotations retain their current behavior. - Parser, analyzer, runtime, editor-display, and regression tests cover union declarations, compatibility, null handling, and runtime validation.
explanation: The requirement is detailed and explicit about union type syntax, semantics, and behavior, making it unambiguous and verifiable through tests and error checks. Although it covers many aspects, they all relate to a single feature, though the breadth of constraints slightly reduces singularity.

requirement: **Requirement ID:** GO-ENCODING-XML-001 **Title:** XML 1.1 Specification Support in encoding/xml  **Description:** The `encoding/xml` package shall support the W3C XML 1.1 (Second Edition) specification for both decoding (parsing) and encoding (generation) operations, while preserving full backward compatibility with XML 1.0.  **Functional Requirements:** 1. **Version Recognition:** The decoder shall accept XML documents declaring `version="1.1"` in the prolog and process them according to XML 1.1 rules; the encoder shall support emitting `<?xml version="1.1" ...?>` declarations when explicitly configured. 2. **Expanded Name Characters:** The parser and encoder shall support the extended set of valid name start and name characters defined in XML 1.1 §2.3 (including supplementary Unicode characters and additional ranges such as U+1F00–U+1FFF). 3. **Control Character Handling:** The decoder shall permit control characters U+0001–U+0008, U+000B–U+000C, and U+000E–U+001F when represented as character references in content and attribute values; the encoder shall escape these characters as character references when generating XML 1.1 output. 4. **Line-End Normalization:** The decoder shall translate U+0085 (NEL) and U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) to U+000A (LF) during line-end processing per XML 1.1 §2.11. 5. **Attribute Value Normalization:** The decoder shall apply XML 1.1 attribute value normalization rules (§3.3.3), which differ from XML 1.0 regarding treatment of whitespace characters and character references. 6. **Compatibility:** Existing behavior for XML 1.0 documents shall remain unchanged; documents without a version declaration or declaring `version="1.0"` shall continue to be processed per XML 1.0 rules.  **Acceptance Criteria:** - [ ] The decoder successfully parses valid XML 1.1 documents containing 1.1-specific name characters, escaped control characters, and NEL/LS line separators. - [ ] The decoder rejects malformed XML 1.1 documents according to XML 1.1 well-formedness and validity constraints. - [ ] The encoder generates well-formed XML 1.1 documents with correct version declarations and proper escaping of 1.1-specific characters. - [ ] All existing XML 1.0 test cases pass without modification. - [ ] New test coverage includes XML 1.1-specific parsing edge cases, line-ending variants, and encoder configuration options.  **Constraints:** - Implementation must adhere to the Go 1 compatibility promise for the standard library. - Performance impact on XML 1.0 document processing shall not exceed 5% compared to the baseline implementation.
explanation: The requirement clearly describes XML 1.1 support and backward compatibility, with detailed functional items and acceptance criteria, though minor ambiguity remains around the encoder configuration flag. It references concrete spec sections and measurable test cases, enabling straightforward verification. requirement: # Requirement: Support Flutter Widgets as Map Markers in `google_maps_flutter`  **ID:** REQ-GMF-WIDGET-MARKERS **Priority:** High **Type:** Functional / Feature Enhancement  ## 1. Statement  The `google_maps_flutter` plugin shall allow developers to use arbitrary Flutter widgets as the visual content of map markers, rendered as interactive, tappable overlays positioned on the map, as an alternative to the existing static `BitmapDescriptor` icons.  ## 2. Background & Rationale  Currently, marker customization is limited to pre-rendered bitmap images (`BitmapDescriptor`), which prevents the use of dynamic, stateful, localized, or themed content on markers. Supporting widgets as markers enables developers to build rich, consistent map UIs (e.g., price badges, live status indicators, animated pins) without off-screen rendering to bitmaps.  ## 3. Functional Requirements  3.1. The `Marker` API shall accept an optional widget specification (e.g., a `WidgetBuilder` or child widget) as an alternative to the existing `icon` parameter. Supplying both shall be a compile-time or runtime error with a clear diagnostic message.  3.2. Widget markers shall be positioned at the marker's geographic coordinates and honor the existing `anchor` parameter for alignment.  3.3. Widget markers shall support the existing marker lifecycle behaviors where platform capabilities allow, including: - `onTap` callbacks with correct hit-testing against the rendered widget bounds; - `z-index` ordering relative to other markers and overlays; - visibility (`visible`), `alpha` (opacity), and `rotation` where supported; - placement relative to `MarkerId`-based updates (add, update, remove) without flicker.  3.4. When the widget subtree rebuilds (e.g., via `setState` or stream updates), the rendered marker content shall update on the map without requiring removal and re-creation of the `Marker`.  3.5. The plugin shall define and document deterministic behavior for widget markers in interaction with info windows, clustering, and dragging, including explicit documentation of any unsupported combinations per platform.  3.6. Existing API usage (markers defined solely with `icon: BitmapDescriptor`) shall remain fully backward compatible with no behavioral changes.  ## 4. Platform Requirements  4.1. The feature shall be implemented for Android and iOS at parity in initial release; web/desktop support shall be documented as supported or explicitly deferred.  4.2. Rendering may be implemented via platform view embedding or rasterization to a texture, provided hit-testing and update requirements (3.3, 3.4) are met.  ## 5. Performance & Constraints  5.1. Map pan/zoom gestures shall remain smooth (no dropped frames beyond an agreed threshold, e.g., maintain ≥ 60 fps on reference devices) with a documented practical limit on the number of simultaneously visible widget markers (target: at least 50).  5.2. Widget markers shall respect the app's theme, text scaling, and localization settings.  ## 6. Acceptance Criteria  - **AC1:** A `Marker` configured with a widget renders the widget at the correct latitude/longitude with the specified anchor alignment on Android and iOS. - **AC2:** Tapping a widget marker triggers its registered `onTap` handler and does not propagate as a map tap. - **AC3:** Changing the widget's internal state (e.g., updating text or color) is reflected on the map within one update cycle, without marker flicker. - **AC4:** Multiple widget markers honor `z-index` ordering and do not interfere with map gesture handling outside their bounds. - **AC5:** Pre-existing icon-based markers compile and behave identically to prior releases (regression-safe).
